name: Jellyscribe
overview: Real-time Letterboxd and Serializd diary sync with duplicate detection
description:
Automatically syncs your Jellyfin watch history to your Letterboxd diary (films) and Serializd diary (TV). Supports multiple users, real-time sync on playback completion, duplicate detection, retry with backoff, and TMDb-based matching.  
  
Universal Repo:  
Generated: 01:23 UTC  
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/builtbyproxy/jellyfin-plugin-letterboxd/main/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/builtbyproxy/jellyfin-plugin-letterboxd

versions.changelog: Films and episodes that Jellyfin marks watched through real playback have always synced with the correct date. But checking a title watched by hand, using the checkmark rather than actually playing it, could leave Jellyfin's own watched-date field set to January 1st 1970 instead of a real date, and the plugin trusted that value as-is. The fix treats an epoch-adjacent watched date the same way it already treats a missing one: there's no real watch date to log yet, so the sync waits rather than posting a bogus entry to Letterboxd or Serializd. Once Jellyfin records an actual playback date for the title, it syncs normally.

When a Letterboxd password goes stale, the plugin no longer retries the login forever. After three consecutive failed logins, syncing for that account pauses itself: no more login attempts (protecting you from Letterboxd rate limiting), a warning appears in Jellyfin's activity log where admins actually look, and the account card in both dashboards shows a "login failing" badge with the date it started. Re-save the account's credentials and syncing resumes on the next run; watches from the paused period are picked up by the scheduled catch-up, so nothing is lost.

The review modal now shows the rating you already gave. Instead of always opening at "No rating", it looks up the rating stored in Jellyfin, whether you set it in the Jellyfin web UI, a client app like Infuse, or an earlier Jellyscribe review, and pre-fills the stars for you, for films, shows, and individual episodes. The star widget also supports half stars now: click the left half of a star for a .5 rating, matching what Letterboxd itself accepts, so a 7/10 in Jellyfin finally displays as the 3.5 stars it really is.

The sidebar link this plugin adds to Jellyfin's nav is injected by registering with the File Transformation plugin once, at Jellyfin startup. That registration was racing File Transformation's own startup init, so on some restarts (including scheduled ones) it silently failed and the link just never appeared, with nothing in the logs beyond a generic, undiagnosable error. Registration now retries a few times before giving up, and a real failure logs the actual cause instead of a useless wrapper message.

Watchlist auto-requests now show up in your sync history. If your watchlist syncs with "auto-request via Jellyseerr" turned on, a successful request used to only ever show up in the server log, there was no way to see it from the dashboard itself. Now every title your watchlist successfully requests (film or TV) gets its own entry in your sync history, with the real title, right alongside your regular Letterboxd and Serializd activity. A request that fails shows up too, so if Jellyseerr rejects something you can see exactly what and when instead of wondering why your watchlist "isn't working."

A few follow-ups to the 2.0.0 rebrand. The admin and user dashboard headers lost their "by Lachlan Young and AI" credit line during the redesign, it's back. The opt-in anonymous telemetry, which only ever counted Letterboxd film syncs, now counts Serializd TV syncs and errors too, since that pipeline was never touched when TV support was built. And the Logs tab's Refresh button, which had been dumping a raw JSON blob into the panel instead of readable log lines, now shows the actual logs.

Two things land together in this release. First, the plugin is renamed from "Letterboxd Sync" to Jellyscribe, a name and a look that actually cover both services it now talks to, instead of the old identity that borrowed Letterboxd's own name and brand colors. Nothing about the rename requires any action, your plugin auto-updates in place, every linked account, sync history entry, and setting carries over untouched, and the repository URL you already have configured does not change.

Second, the plugin no longer stops at films. Link a Serializd account on the new TV / Serializd tab and TV episodes sync to Serializd automatically, watched status in real time as you finish an episode, with a daily catch-up for anything missed and a Sync TV Now button to run it on demand, each entry dated to when you actually watched it rather than when the sync ran.

Star ratings and favorites mirror to Serializd's rating and like, and you can post a written review straight from the dashboard, at the show or episode level. Your Serializd watchlist syncs back into Jellyfin too, as a browsable collection and a playable episode queue, with an optional Jellyseerr auto-request for anything still missing from your library.

Films still go to Letterboxd exactly as before, the two are completely independent, so a Serializd hiccup never touches your Letterboxd sync. Each Jellyfin user links their own Serializd account (by email or username), and passwords are encrypted at rest the same way Letterboxd credentials are.

If the "Import Letterboxd diary as Jellyfin watched" task ran and did nothing, it used to finish in a second and leave no trace in the log, so a switched-off toggle looked identical to a broken feature. The task now says why it skipped each user (for example, an account exists but diary import is not turned on, with a pointer to the setting), reports when your Letterboxd returned no films, and always ends with a one-line summary of what it checked. A stuck progress banner on the dashboard for empty diaries is also fixed. If reverse sync has not been working for you, update, run the task once, and the log will now tell you exactly why.

**"Send logs to developer" now tells you when there is nothing to send.** Previously, if the plugin had not logged anything recently, the send dialog reported success but the bundle arrived empty, and neither you nor the developer could tell why. The dialog now warns you when no plugin log lines were found, with a hint to reproduce the problem first and send again, and every bundle includes a small status line saying which log files were read and how many lines matched, so support requests no longer dead-end on an empty bundle.
Docs-only; ships no release.

A small improvement to the opt-in anonymous telemetry: alongside the existing per-week sync bucket, the weekly ping now includes a lifetime sync bucket. Until now, an instance reporting zero syncs in a week was indistinguishable from one where syncing never worked at all; the lifetime bucket separates the two, so setup problems can be spotted and fixed. Same privacy rules as everything else: a coarse bucket only (0, 1-10, 11-100, 100+), never exact numbers, and nothing is sent unless you opted in.

Your Letterboxd password, session cookies, and Seerr API key are now encrypted before they are written to disk, instead of sitting in the plugin config file as plaintext. Nothing changes about how you use the plugin: existing saved credentials are picked up and upgraded automatically the next time they are saved, no re-entry needed.

No functional changes to syncing. The project now documents openly how it is built: a new AI.md page explains that most of the plugin is AI-written under human direction and review, what tooling is used, and the checks every change passes before it ships. The Code of Conduct is rewritten to something honest for a one-person project, and the README links to all of it.

A second repository entry for this plugin, an edge-cached mirror of the exact same manifest, is added to your Jellyfin catalog next to the existing GitHub one, a single time. Your GitHub entry is never touched, so updates keep working even if the mirror is unreachable, and if you would rather not have the mirror you can simply delete it: the plugin will not add it back. The mirror counts an anonymous, weekly-rotating hash per request so we can see roughly how many servers run the plugin; no IP addresses or personal data are ever stored, and this is entirely separate from the opt-in telemetry. The mirror also no longer caches upstream GitHub errors at the edge, so a brief GitHub hiccup cannot pin a failed response for other users.

No functional changes to syncing. This release adds an anonymous, privacy-preserving install counter so the developer can see roughly how many Jellyfin servers run the plugin. No personal data is collected: your IP address is never stored, and the anonymous weekly fingerprint used to avoid double-counting cannot be traced back to you or linked across weeks.

Fixes a sync failure introduced when Letterboxd changed their website. Films stopped logging to your diary because the plugin could no longer read each film's identifier from its Letterboxd page. The plugin now reads the new page format, so watched films sync again.
test: strip instance_id before payload raw-count assertions to fix random-GUID flake

Jellyseerr and Overseerr have merged into a single project called Seerr. The plugin now uses the new name everywhere you see it, in the settings page, your personal account page, and the documentation, so the labels match what you see in the app you are connecting to. Nothing about the integration changes: your existing Seerr URL, API key, and per-account settings are kept, and there is nothing to reconfigure.
No functional changes. CI now uploads JUnit test results to Codecov Test Analytics so flaky tests and failures are tracked across releases. Nothing in the plugin itself changes.

Letterboxd often blocks plain username/password login with a Cloudflare or reCAPTCHA challenge, and accounts with two-factor authentication can never log in that way at all. This release makes raw cookies the clearly recommended way to authenticate, warns you when you save an account without them, and turns the cryptic two-factor login failure into a message that tells you exactly what to do.

- Raw Cookies are now presented as the recommended way to authenticate, on both the admin settings page and your personal account page, with a short explanation of why password-only login is unreliable.
- Saving an enabled account that has a password but no raw cookies now shows a non-blocking warning, so you find out before the first sync fails. The save still goes through.
- Accounts with two-factor authentication enabled now fail login with a clear, actionable message instead of a vague generic error, telling you to add raw cookies (including cf_clearance) or disable 2FA.

**Send your logs to the developer in one click.** Reporting a problem with Letterboxd Sync used to mean digging through Jellyfin's log files and pasting the right lines into a GitHub issue. This release adds a **"Send logs to developer"** button to the Logs tab that does it for you.

**What it does**
- Click the button and the plugin bundles your recent Letterboxd Sync log lines (the same ones already shown on the Logs tab) and uploads them privately, then hands you a short **reference code** like `LBX-7Q2F9K`. Quote that code when you open a GitHub issue and the developer can pull your exact logs, no more copy-pasting walls of text.
- A confirmation step lets you **preview exactly what will be sent** (the real log lines and a telemetry snapshot, byte-for-byte what gets uploaded) and add a short note describing what went wrong.

**Privacy, stated plainly**
- Unlike the anonymous weekly telemetry from 1.16.0, **logs are not anonymous**: they can contain your Letterboxd username or film titles, and the bundle is linked to your install's telemetry ID. The dialog says this before you send, nothing leaves your server until you confirm, and passwords, cookies, and auth tokens are never logged.
- Works whether or not you have anonymous telemetry enabled. Uploaded bundles are stored privately and **auto-deleted after 90 days**.

**Also in this release**
- **Stronger log access control:** the plugin's log endpoint now requires administrator access. Previously any signed-in Jellyfin user could read the Letterboxd Sync logs (which name every linked Letterboxd account and watched film); on shared or family servers this is now admin-only.
- Better diagnostics when you do send logs: full multi-line error traces are captured intact (they were previously fragmented), log text is cleaned of stray terminal control codes, and the bundle always records your Jellyfin version.

Nothing changes unless you choose to use the new button.

New: anonymous, opt-in usage telemetry — off by default, enabled via a one-time dashboard banner or Settings. One small bucketed ping a week (versions, enabled features, size buckets; never film titles, usernames, IPs, or exact numbers), a Preview-exact-JSON button showing precisely what's sent, a regenerable random instance ID, and an extra capped ping when errors start occurring so fleet-wide breakage is caught early. Full payload documented in the README. No other behaviour changes.

Fixes the plugin failing to load (showing as disabled) on Jellyfin 10.11.9 and 10.11.10 for versions v1.14.1 through v1.15.3: those releases were compiled against a newer Jellyfin SDK than the advertised minimum. The plugin is now always compiled against the oldest supported Jellyfin SDK, a policy enforced by CI, so the advertised minimum version is the real one. If your plugin recently stopped working, update to this version and restart Jellyfin. No feature changes.

Adds the design spec for upcoming anonymous, opt-in usage telemetry (minimal bucketed payload, off by default, one-time prompt, full payload preview) and an automated regression canary. Spec only; no telemetry code or behaviour changes in this release.
Maintenance: fixes an intermittent CI-only test failure where a background sync spawned by one test could still hold the sync gate when the next test ran. No plugin behaviour changes.
Documentation: the Releases page on letterboxdsync.dev now has structured highlights for v1.13.4 through v1.15.0. No plugin behaviour changes.

New opt-in per-account setting "Also backfill requests for already-available watchlist films": creates attributed Jellyseerr requests for watchlist films that entered the library without one, so "who requested this?" is always answerable. Off by default; existing behavior unchanged.
build: Bump Jellyfin.Controller and Jellyfin.Model
fix(sync): skip films with no LastPlayedDate and abandon films after 3 consecutive failures
test: expand plugin coverage to 89.8% line / 81.4% branch

Maintenance release. Two preventative changes aimed at the next Jellyfin SDK ABI surprise. Dependabot now watches the `Jellyfin.Controller` and `Jellyfin.Model` packages and opens a PR the day a new patch ships, so any breaking ABI change is caught by CI on our timeline rather than via a user bug report (the v1.13.0 fix only existed because Jellyfin 10.11.9's silent removal of `IUserManager.Users` surfaced as bigrichwood's report). And the version-gate CI check now refuses a patch-only version bump when `targetAbi.txt` changes in the same PR, because moving the Jellyfin compatibility floor stops a cohort of users from being offered the next plugin update and that warrants at least a minor bump so the change shows up clearly in the release notes. No plugin behaviour changes.

Maintenance release. The manifest changelog field and the letterboxdsync.dev Releases page now match the v1.0–v1.12 single-paragraph user-facing prose style after v1.13.0 (rendered as a multi-paragraph incident report) and v1.13.1 (rendered as the raw conventional-commit subject line) drifted away from it. The release workflow now pulls the manifest changelog from a `## Release notes` section in the merged PR's body via the GitHub API, so the prose that lands in users' plugin catalogs is deliberate and reviewable. Backfills the two missing structured entries on the Releases page and rewrites the two stale manifest entries inline. No plugin behaviour changes.

Maintenance release: stronger release pipeline. Every PR now bumps the version (gated by a required CI check) and auto-ships on merge to main, PR titles must follow Conventional Commits, and letterboxdsync.dev rebuilds on every release. No plugin behaviour changes. Past incident behind this work: v1.13.0 was cut manually after merge and the site Releases page was stale through both v1.12.0 and v1.13.0 because the manifest auto-commit could not trigger Deploy site.

Required update for Jellyfin 10.11.9 and newer. Jellyfin 10.11.9 removed the Users property from IUserManager and replaced it with a GetUsers() method, so the plugin (compiled against the 10.11.0 SDK) threw MissingMethodException on every user-list read on 10.11.9 and 10.11.10. Symptoms before this fix: the dashboard Stats and History endpoints returned 500, the Sync watched movies to Letterboxd scheduled task failed immediately, and Sync Letterboxd watchlist to playlist failed the same way. Plugin behaviour is otherwise unchanged from v1.12.0. targetAbi is now 10.11.9.0, so Jellyfin 10.11.0 through 10.11.8 servers stay on v1.12.0 via the catalog gate; upgrade Jellyfin to 10.11.9 or newer to receive future plugin updates. Fixes #46.

Multi-account support: one Jellyfin user can now link multiple Letterboxd accounts. Auto-sync (real-time on playback completion and scheduled) fans out across every enabled account, with per-account failures isolated. Manual /Sync, /SyncWatchlist, and /Review endpoints accept an optional letterboxdUsername selector and fan out by default when omitted. Diary import unions played-state across all accounts and merges ratings with the primary account winning conflicts (existing Jellyfin ratings are still preserved). Watchlist playlists are now per-account (default name: 'Letterboxd Watchlist ({letterboxdUsername})', overridable per account). New IsPrimary flag on each account, normalised on save (at most one primary per Jellyfin user). UI: the sidebar 'My Letterboxd' page now has feature parity with the admin page for per-account management (add, remove, test, configure every account belonging to your Jellyfin user without admin access). Review modal exposes a 'Post as' account selector when more than one account is enabled, defaulting to all accounts. Behaviour change: existing single-account users will see a new per-account watchlist playlist created on first sync after upgrade, the old 'Letterboxd Watchlist' playlist is left untouched.

Docs: when a Cloudflare 403 happens after you've already pasted Raw Cookies and a matching User-Agent, the plugin error message and README now explain why (cf_clearance is short-lived, pinned to the IP that solved the challenge, and the connection itself is TLS-fingerprinted) and what to try. Addresses the dead-end case reported in #34. No plugin behaviour changes.

Fix: with diary-import enabled, the daily sync was posting phantom rewatch entries to Letterboxd for films you had only marked played via diary import (never actually watched on Jellyfin). The runner now suppresses these films until a real Jellyfin playback sets a LastPlayedDate, at which point the rewatch lands on Letterboxd as expected. Docs: install instructions now call out the File Transformation plugin as a prerequisite for the in-sidebar Letterboxd link.

Fix: watchlisting a TV show on Letterboxd no longer auto-requests an unrelated movie in Jellyseerr. TMDb has independent ID namespaces for movies and TV (e.g. tv/198102 = Hijack, movie/198102 = Cutie Honey Flash), and the link extractor was treating every tmdb link as a movie ID. Now skips links whose URL points at /tv/. Adds regression coverage for the mismatch.

Bidirectional rating sync: dashboard reviews mirror their star rating into Jellyfin's UserItemData.Rating (always overwrites), and the daily diary import seeds Jellyfin ratings from Letterboxd for films that don't yet have a Jellyfin rating (anti-clobber). Switched the diary import API path from /log-entries to /films?memberRelationship=Watched so films you rated on Letterboxd without logging a watch now sync too. New in-dashboard Logs tab with per-user and free-text filters, copy-to-clipboard, and download-as-.log for support requests. Privacy hardening: review text is no longer logged.
Maintenance: bump GitHub Actions runtime versions (checkout v6, setup-dotnet v5, action-gh-release v3) to remain on a supported Node version. No plugin behaviour changes.

Mirror Letterboxd watchlist into Jellyseerr's user watchlist (per-account toggle, two-way sync, movies-only so manually-added Jellyseerr TV is safe). On-demand 'Sync Watchlist Now' button on the plugin dashboard so you don't have to wait for the daily run. Pre-flight check against Jellyseerr's media status eliminates duplicate requests on every run (was creating fresh requests for already-pending/processing/available titles). Per-user watchlist sync runner extracted with a shared SyncGate so diary and watchlist syncs serialise.

Local-history duplicate backstop: refuse to MarkAsWatched when sync history shows a recent successful sync that does not pass the rewatch threshold, fixes the Cloudflare-failed-validator path that was creating real Letterboxd diary duplicates. Paginated dashboard history table (100 per page) now that the 500-entry cap is gone. Addresses #21.

Skip already-synced films using local sync history so we don't burn Cloudflare quota on duplicate checks; prioritise previously-failed/skipped films first; per-account stop-on-failure toggle to halt the moment Letterboxd anti-flooding triggers; explicit info-level logging for every skip with reason; non-admin users can now Run Sync Now (triggers their account only). Fixes #20.
Jellyseerr auto-request for unmatched watchlist films (per-user attribution via Jellyfin User ID), plus dedup fix so the watchlist playlist no longer accumulates duplicate entries on each run
Per-account User-Agent override so Cloudflare cookies copied from any browser (Chrome, Safari, etc.) work without UA mismatch
Fix review posting via official API: resolve film LID from TMDb ID instead of slug (fixes #12)
Official Letterboxd API integration (primary) with web scraping fallback, eliminates Cloudflare 403 errors
User self-service account setup, sidebar link for all users, test connection button, standalone user page via File Transformation injection
Architecture refactor, TMDb cache, progress dashboard, diary import fix, Cloudflare resilience, watchlist cleanup
Real-time playback sync via PlaybackHandler, automatic session re-auth on 401
Fix sync history persistence across version upgrades
Star ratings in reviews, rewatch date picker, Cloudflare retry on reviews, better error display, sync history persistence fix
Dashboard with sync history, watchlist sync, diary import, reviews, Cloudflare backoff, rating sync, rewatch detection
Initial release: real-time sync, scheduled catch-up, multi-user, duplicate detection, retry with backoff

## Release v0.7.1.0

###  Dieses Update führt ein völlig neues System zur Pfadverwaltung ein, macht die Suche deutlich mächtiger und verbessert die Benutzererfahrung durch eine direkte Videovorschau.

 ## 🚀 Neue Funktionen
   * Kontextbasiertes Pfad-Management: Anstelle eines einzigen globalen Download-Ordners können nun spezifische Standardpfade für verschiedene Mediathek-Inhalte festgelegt werden:
       * Filme & Serien: Getrennte Basisordner ermöglichen eine saubere, automatische Integration in die jeweilige Jellyfin-Bibliothek.
       * Abonnements & Manuelle Downloads: Eigene Zielverzeichnisse sorgen für eine bessere Organisation Ihrer Medien.
   * Direkte Videovorschau (Play-Button): Suchergebnisse verfügen nun über einen Play-Button. Damit lassen sich die MP4-Direktlinks der Sender sofort im Browser öffnen, um Inhalte vor dem Download kurz zu sichten.
   * Intelligente Sucherweiterung:
       * Kombinierte Abfragen: Die Suche erlaubt nun die gleichzeitige Eingabe von Titel und Thema, um Treffer in großen Mediatheken (z.B. ARD/ZDF) präziser einzugrenzen.
       * Auto-Pre-Fill: Der Dialog für erweiterte Downloads wird jetzt automatisch mit erkannten Metadaten und Pfadvorschlägen (basierend auf der Videoanalyse) vorausgefüllt.
       * Optimierte Eingabe: Suchfelder wachsen nun dynamisch mit dem Text mit (auto-grow).
   * UI-Verbesserungen: Die Standard-Pfadeinstellungen in der Konfiguration sind jetzt einklappbar, um die Übersichtlichkeit zu erhöhen.

 ## 🛠️ Verbesserungen & Refactoring
   * Restrukturierung der Web-UI: Komplette Trennung von HTML-Struktur und JavaScript-Logik zur Verbesserung der Wartbarkeit und Ladezeiten.
   * Robuste Verzeichniserstellung: Die Logik zur automatischen Erstellung von Jellyfin-konformen Ordnerstrukturen wurde grundlegend verbessert.
   * Metadaten-Logik: Verfeinerte Integration von DuckDuckGo und TMDB-Suchen für eine bessere Zuordnung von Postern und Beschreibungen.

 ## 🐞 Bugfixes
   * Sicherheits-Update: Implementierung eines Schutzes gegen Path-Traversal-Angriffe bei der manuellen Pfadeingabe für Downloads.

## v0.3.0.0 - Automated Cleanup, Enhanced Subscriptions & Refactoring

  This release brings significant improvements to subscription management, file maintenance, and the underlying architecture of the plugin.

 ### 🚀 New Features

   * Automated `.strm` Cleanup: A new scheduled task scans your download directories for invalid .strm files. It safely deletes files only if the stream URL is definitively gone (404/410), keeping your library clean without
     risking accidental deletions during server outages.
   * Subscription Management: You can now enable or disable individual subscriptions without deleting them.
   * Smart Duplicate Detection: The plugin now scans the target directory for existing episodes (SxxExx or absolute numbering) to prevent redundant downloads.
   * Library Scan Toggle: Added an option to choose whether the Jellyfin library should be scanned automatically after a download finishes.
   * Enhanced Extras Handling: Better detection and handling of non-episode content (Trailers, Interviews) with options to save them as separate .strm files.

 ### 🐛 Bug Fixes & Improvements

   * Language Detection: Fixed an issue where short words in titles were misinterpret as language codes.
   * API Stability: Fixed API response mapping (replaced missing Total field with QueryInfo).

 ### 🛠 Technical Improvements

   * Major Refactoring: The download logic has been split into SubscriptionProcessor and DownloadManager for better stability and maintainability.
   * Frontend Modernization: Refactored the configuration page to use ES6 classes and safer DOM manipulation.
   * Grouped Downloads: Video and subtitle downloads are now grouped into a single logical job.

name: Last.fm
description:
Scrobble Last.fm plays with Jellyfin  
  
Universal Repo:  
Generated: 01:23 UTC  
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielfariati/jellyfin-plugin-lastfm/refs/heads/master/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/danielfariati/jellyfin-plugin-lastfm
overview: A plugin that scrobbles your Jellyfin music to Last.fm

versions.changelog: Fix for tracks without album artist metadata.
Fixed audiobooks being incorrectly treated as music and sent to Last.fm as now playing tracks, scrobbles, or favourite updates.

Scrobble log messages now include the exact data sent to Last.fm, url encoded and without the credentials, so a rejected scrobble can be replayed as is. This also covers the album artist and the MusicBrainz id, which were never logged before, and makes characters that are invisible in a log, such as non breaking spaces in artist names, easy to spot. This only changes logging, scrobbling behaviour is unchanged.

Playback events received from Jellyfin are now logged, in both the default and the alternative mode, to help debug reports of tracks that never get scrobbled. Some clients do not tell the server that a track was played or stopped, and until now there was no way to tell that apart from the plugin discarding the event. The reason a track was skipped is logged as well. This only adds logging, scrobbling behaviour is unchanged.

Scrobbles that Last.fm silently drops are now logged as warnings with the reason, instead of being reported as successful. Last.fm answers those with a normal HTTP 200 and no error code, so they were previously indistinguishable from accepted scrobbles in the logs. This does not change which scrobbles are accepted, it only makes the rejected ones visible.

This version requires Jellyfin 10.11.9 or newer. Jellyfin 10.11.9 changed an internal API the plugin relies on. Fixes the 'Import Last.fm Loved Tracks' task. Also refactored the settings page to use plugin-specific element IDs, avoiding clashes with other plugins' configuration pages - this might fix the user dropdown showing up empty for some users.

New API key and secret, since the previous one was blocked or deleted by the original project owner. After upgrading, every user will need to re-enter their credentials for the plugin to work again. There's no way to migrate the old credentials since the API key is different and we don't store the actual user password (we just use it to create a session key). This is a necessary change to keep the plugin working, since the stored session keys were generated with the previous API key that is not valid anymore.
Allowing to change the API Host (Libre.fm support) + Masking password in config page
Naming convention fixes
Fixed Jellyfin version support checks, naming consistencies and plugin ID usage
Prevent duplicate scrobbles by ignoring repeats within 15s

versions.changelog:
## v1.6.6.0
### Fixes
- The lyrics task no longer re-downloads tracks that already have synced lyrics on disk. When a track's lyrics were saved but the database still reported them as plain (Jellyfin doesn't refresh metadata after a download until the next library scan), the task kept "upgrading" the same tracks on every run. It now trusts the synced .lrc file already on disk and skips it. -> #43

## v1.6.5.0
### Fixes
- Build against Jellyfin 10.11.6 instead of always the latest release. Previous builds were linked against 10.11.10 assemblies, which made Jellyfin report the plugin as "not supported" (TypeLoadException) on older 10.11.x servers. The plugin is now compatible with Jellyfin 10.11.6 and newer. -> #55

## v1.6.4.0
### Fixes
- Lyric file detection now also checks Jellyfin's internal metadata folder, not just the media folder. With "Save lyrics into media folders" disabled, already-downloaded lyrics are detected instead of being re-downloaded on every task run, which also reduces load on lrclib.net -> #54

## v1.6.3.0
### What's New
- Optional self-hosted LRCLIB server URL: point the plugin at your own LRCLIB instance instead of lrclib.net. Subpath URLs are preserved and the URL is validated on save. Thanks to @Nausi-llon (#50).
- Built-in rate limiting for lrclib.net requests: enforces a 200 ms minimum gap between calls and honors HTTP 429 `Retry-After` so transient spikes back off cleanly instead of surfacing as per-track errors.
- Identifiable User-Agent on every lrclib request (`jellyfin-plugin-lyrics/<version> (+repo-url)`) so the LRCLIB operators can distinguish this plugin from `jellyfin/jellyfin-plugin-lrclib` (#49).

### Notes
- No configuration changes required for existing users — the self-host URL defaults to `https://lrclib.net` and the rate limit only kicks in under load.

## v1.6.2.0
### What's New
- Auto-removes the official "LrcLib Lyrics" plugin (`jellyfin-plugin-lrclib`) on startup if installed, since both plugins register the same lyrics provider and conflict. This plugin is a fork that fixes critical issues — see README. The old plugin can be reinstalled later to switch back.

## v1.6.1.0
### What's New
- Lyrics alternative discovery: skip re-downloading lyrics that already failed in a previous run
- Synced-lyric upgrade now checks the existing sidecar file before replacing plain text

### Fixes
- Stop matching instrumental tracks against unrelated songs: honor LRCLIB's instrumental flag, validate every match against requested duration and artist, and drop the track-name-only fuzzy fallback when artist info is available (#40)
- Scheduled task log: split DB-desync skips from "already synced" skips so plain `.txt` sidecars are no longer counted as synced

### Settings
- New configurable duration-tolerance filter (default on, ±15s) with UI toggle to tune or disable

### Notes
- Jellyfin 10.11.6 or newer is now recommended (see README)

## v1.6.0.0
### What's New
- Added song title cleanup to strip YouTube-style suffixes (Official Music Video, etc.) and duplicate artist names
- Added progressive search fallback: retries with fewer parameters when no results are found
- Added multi-artist support: splits "artist1/artist2" and tries each artist individually
- Replace non-synced lyrics with synced ones when available
- Sped up scheduled lyrics task

### Fixes
- Fixed DI issue with RetryStateStore causing plugin to malfunction on startup
- Fixed fuzzy search failing when album name is missing
- Fixed crash on missing artist or invalid id

### Defaults Changed
- Strict search is now disabled by default
- "Exclude album name" is now enabled by default

## v1.5.0.0
### What's New
- Fixed support for Jellyfin 10.11

## v1.4.0.0
### What's New
- Added support for Jellyfin 10.11

## v1.3.0.0
### What's New
- Fixed a lot of plugin loading issues
- Fixed GitHub Action Workflows

### Technical Improvements
- Consistent versioning across all project files
- Better package compatibility with Jellyfin 10.9.x series
- Improved documentation and installation instructions

name: SponsorBlock
description:
Skip sponsored segments in YouTube videos using SponsorBlock data.  
  
Universal Repo:  
Generated: 01:23 UTC  
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/felixfoertsch/jellyfin-sponsorblock/main/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/felixfoertsch/jellyfin-sponsorblock

versions.changelog: Add an opt-in Jellyfin metadata source for YouTube IDs. Preserve filename and custom-regex matching as the default, read validated Youtube provider IDs imported from NFO uniqueid metadata, and expose the source choice in plugin settings.

Add Jellyfin 12 support. Retarget to .NET 10 and Jellyfin Controller 12.0.0-rc3, implement the new media-segment cleanup contract, and preserve the event-driven SponsorBlock workflow without enabling the core library segment scan.
Serialize SponsorBlock processing to avoid concurrent refresh and playback work for the same item. Bump the plugin version for local installation.

Add Done state with convergence-based polling. Videos older than 30 days (by YouTube publish date) are fetched once and frozen. Videos younger than 30 days are polled daily until segment data is unchanged for 5 consecutive checks, then frozen. Stale segments are now deleted when SponsorBlock data disappears. Daily scan task refactored to a clean two-phase dispatcher.

Add dedicated SponsorBlock log file (log_SponsorBlock_YYYYMMDD.log) in Jellyfin's log directory. All info/warning/error events now write to both the main server log and the dedicated file, so the plugin appears as a separate log entry in the Jellyfin dashboard.

Add comprehensive logging to the orchestrator and triggers. Every decision point (scope check, path empty, ID extraction failure, state-machine skip, segment write, state transition) now logs at information or debug level, so issues are diagnosable directly from the Jellyfin log dashboard.
Fix EnumerateScoped to discover Episode and Movie items, not just standalone Video. YouTube libraries imported as TV Shows store items as Episode type, which BaseItemKind.Video did not match.

Fix automatic loading for old archives and restore DLL-only release packaging. The daily refresh now discovers selected-library videos older than the sanity-check window, old untracked items use their Jellyfin DateCreated for the 48-hour decision, and NoData rows recheck after cooldown instead of being terminal.

Add a one-shot Force Scan button for existing archives. Admins can backfill every video in the selected libraries once, while the normal daily refresh stays limited to tracked Pending and HasData items. Includes duplicate-scan protection and status endpoints.

Repair pruned SponsorBlock segments on playback. When Jellyfin refreshes a changed media file it can delete generated MediaSegment rows while the plugin state still says HasData; playback start now verifies that Jellyfin still has segment rows and re-fetches/recreates them if they were pruned.

Fix delayed SponsorBlock loading. Register the daily refresh scheduled task so Pending items are retried automatically, correct the 24-hour playback retry condition, and wait for playback-start processing so freshly fetched segments can reach the first playback session.

Actually fix segments not reaching clients. Jellyfin's IMediaSegmentManager.CreateSegmentAsync expects the second arg to be the MD5-derived provider id (new Guid(MD5(name.ToLowerInvariant() UTF-16 LE)).ToString("N")), not the literal provider name. We were passing "SponsorBlock" verbatim, so stored segments didn't match any registered provider and the public MediaSegments API filtered them out. Pre-compute the hash and pass that. After upgrading, hit Reset on the config page so old segments get re-fetched under the correct provider id.

Fix segments not reaching clients. v1.1.0.0 dropped the IMediaSegmentProvider registration to avoid the slow scan, but Jellyfin filters segments by registered provider, so stored segments were never served. Re-register a stub provider (Supports => false, GetMediaSegments => empty) so Jellyfin recognizes 'SponsorBlock' as a known provider while the orchestrator stays in charge of fetching.

Add admin Reset button on the plugin config page that wipes SponsorBlock state and owned segments for items in the configured library scope, so the orchestrator re-fetches on next playback. Useful for re-fetching items whose SponsorBlock data became available after the initial scan.

Replace media-segment scan with event-driven orchestrator. Add daily refresh task at configurable hour. Add per-library scoping (empty by default — admin must opt in). SQLite per-item state machine (Pending/HasData/NoData) with 48h sanity check.
Remove non-functional user segment actions table from config page.
Initial release.

name: Native Trickplay
description:
Generates HLS I-frame variants so Apple TV / AVPlayer clients get native
scrubbing thumbnails on the transport bar — no client-side overlay needed.
One-time ffmpeg cost per item, then cached.
Includes a configurable daily prune scheduled task (orphan removal,
age-based eviction, optional LRU size cap) so the cache doesn't grow
unbounded.  
  
Universal Repo:  
Generated: 01:23 UTC  
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HarshLabs/jellyfin-plugin-native-trickplay/main/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/HarshLabs/jellyfin-plugin-native-trickplay
overview: Native HLS trickplay for AVPlayer-based clients (Apple TV).

versions.changelog:
- Fixed: trickplay playlists and image segments now enforce each user's library access and parental controls. Previously, any signed-in user could request the scrubbing thumbnails of items outside their allowed libraries.
- Improved: the dashboard's item list loads dramatically faster on large libraries (it no longer reads every cached playlist from disk just to show cache status).
- Improved: changing "Concurrent encodes" now takes effect immediately — no server restart needed.
- Fixed: corrupt video files could make HDR detection time out, producing washed-out thumbnails for HDR content.
- Fixed: searching with an extremely large season or episode number could error the item list.
- Hardened the release pipeline: build steps are now pinned to exact, immutable versions.

After updating, restart your server once as usual. No cache regeneration is required.

If you reinstall Jellyfin (or its database gets rebuilt) and point the plugin back at your existing cache folder, the plugin now relinks every cached entry to your library automatically — no re-encoding, no lost cache.

- New: orphaned cache entries (from a reinstall or database rebuild) are automatically relinked to your items at server startup and before every scheduled prune run.
- New: the dashboard shows a warning banner with a one-click "Relink orphaned entries" button whenever orphaned entries are detected.
- Fixed: Cache Status no longer counts orphaned entries as cached (previously it could show 100% coverage while every item listed as "not cached" and playback re-encoded).
- Fixed: the daily prune task no longer deletes a reinstalled server's still-valid cache — it relinks first and only removes entries that truly match nothing.

Update, restart your server once, and your cache reconnects on its own within about 30 seconds — or press the new Relink button on the plugin dashboard.

Fixes playback stalling on Apple TV when audio is passed through unchanged (stream copy). The playlist could advertise the wrong audio format, which made the player wait forever for audio it was never going to get. If playback ever froze right after turning subtitles off, this is that fix.
Fixed playback breaking on SDR variable-bitrate files when trickplay is enabled. Affected videos could freeze mid-playback or get stuck on a loading screen when resumed; they now play normally.

* On HDR sources, tone mapping now runs on the GPU when your ffmpeg build supports it (OpenCL for Intel QSV / VAAPI / AMD on Linux, CUDA for NVIDIA, Metal on macOS). The previous CPU tone-mapping path was the dominant cost on HDR content — moving it to the GPU is the bulk of the speedup. Falls back to the old CPU path automatically when no GPU tone-mapping filter is available.

* The ffmpeg filter chain now thins frames down to the trickplay rate (one every couple of seconds) before any per-frame work runs. Previously every decoded frame was transferred GPU → CPU before being discarded — for a 2-hour 4K HDR source that's hundreds of thousands of wasted full-resolution transfers.

* New "GPU tone-mapping for HDR" toggle in the plugin settings, on by default. Disable it if GPU tone-mapping misbehaves on your hardware — encodes still benefit from the filter-chain reorder.

* Encodes that hit a GPU tone-mapping issue now fall back to CPU tone-mapping automatically (keeping hardware decode), and only drop to full software decode if the hardware decoder itself fails. The dashboard's hardware-path column shows what's actually in use (e.g. "QSV+OCL", "VideoToolbox+VT") so you can see the path each encode is taking.

A user on an Intel iGPU reported that a 2-hour 4K HDR film took ~90 minutes to generate on the prior version. The same encode finishes in roughly 10 minutes on this version.

Previously, if you deleted a library from Jellyfin, the plugin's
"Find & select items" list and the daily pre-generation task kept
seeing items from the removed library until Jellyfin's next library
scan cleaned them up — which meant inflated totals on the dashboard
and the nightly task wasting time encoding files that were no longer
in any library.

The plugin now scopes its lookups to the libraries currently visible
in Jellyfin, so the moment you remove a library the dashboard total
matches the Cache Status widget and the pre-gen task stops touching
those items.

No action required — just update the plugin and the next dashboard
load will reflect the correct counts.

Avoids advertising an iframe trickplay variant whose playlist resolves
to a valid-but-empty stub on cache miss — that combination can stall
AVPlayer on tvOS 26 with seek-shifted on-demand transcodes. Trickplay
appears on the next playback session once the warmup task generates
the cache.

* Search results above 200 items now load progressively. Default page is 500; 'Load more' appends the next batch and 'Load all' pulls everything matching the current filter.
* New 'Select all N items matching this filter' link appears once you've checked some visible items in a paginated result. Click it to select every match — including items not yet rendered. The bulk Generate or Evict action then operates on the entire match set, not just the page in front of you.
* Selection persists across pagination — checking an item on page 1 stays checked when you load page 2.
* 'Clear selection' link in the banner dismisses an all-matching selection. Filter, sort, or search changes also reset selection automatically.

Cancel active encodings

* New "Cancel" button on each in-flight row in the Encoding-in-progress panel, plus a "Cancel all" button in the footer.
* Works for both queued items (waiting for an encoder slot) and items currently being encoded.
* Existing cached trickplay for the canceled item is preserved — only the in-progress attempt is dropped.
* Cancel is idempotent — a second click is harmless.

Release notes now reflect actual changes per release. Prior versions all showed "Initial release" due to a publishing oversight.

overview: Fornisce titoli, trame, generi, valutazioni e cover art in italiano per anime, utilizzando AnimeClick.it come fonte.

versions.changelog: Via il tetto di 200 episodi: il ricontrollo dei titoli lavora tutto l'arretrato, protetto dal ritardo fra le richieste. I titoli mancanti sono divisi fra recuperabili, in attesa della fonte e non recuperabili. La pagina perde contatori e pulsanti superflui: i numeri filtrano con un clic e la selezione manuale resta solo sui titoli incerti.

Completare le sinossi è un clic solo: «Completa tutte le sinossi» avvia un'attività che procede a lotti e si ferma da sola quando non resta niente su cui agire, continuando anche a pagina chiusa. La stessa attività è pianificata ogni settimana.

Le sinossi degli episodi tornano anche per gli anime lunghi tenuti in una sola stagione: il numero assoluto pubblicato da TheTVDB viene letto senza richieste aggiuntive e su TMDB viene tradotto nella coppia stagione/episodio reale, solo quando la coordinata richiesta non può esistere.

L'audit ricorda l'esito di ogni riparazione: le sinossi che nessuna fonte ha escono dal lotto automatico invece di essere riproposte a vuoto, quelle in attesa di traduzione non vengono riaccodate e il lotto si distribuisce fra le serie.
Audit libreria più leggibile su desktop e mobile, con ricerca, filtri, sezioni progressive e controlli bulk sicuri per titoli e sinossi.
Audit qualità della libreria e riparazione sicura delle sinossi; abbinamento episodi e stagioni più rigoroso; coda traduzioni AI resiliente con refresh Overview-only; cache e invalidazione corrette.

v0.5.0.0: rilascio di funzionalità. La traduzione automatica non è più legata a un solo fornitore: il servizio si sceglie da un menu fra Ollama (in rete o in casa), OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Mistral, Groq, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Together, xAI Grok, LM Studio o qualunque endpoint compatibile OpenAI. Il nome del modello non ha più un valore predefinito, di proposito: i fornitori li ritirano e rinominano, quindi il plugin chiede l'elenco al servizio con il pulsante «Elenca modelli». Chi aveva già configurato Ollama non deve fare niente, il profilo salvato viene travasato al primo avvio. Non è possibile usare un abbonamento ChatGPT o Claude al posto di una chiave API: l'API è fatturata a parte e Anthropic vieta l'uso dei token dei piani consumer fuori dai suoi programmi. Nuova scheda Libreria: analizza la copertura dei titoli leggendo solo le schede già in cache, quindi senza richieste ad AnimeClick, e per ogni serie e stagione dice quale delle nove cause spiega un titolo mancante, con i pulsanti per rileggere la scheda, svuotarne la cache o avviare subito il ricontrollo. Il ricontrollo settimanale ora sceglie con la stessa classificazione, invece di spendere il budget sulle schede che non pubblicano titoli e di ignorare per sempre gli episodi mai abbinati. Corretti due abbinamenti: uno spin-off numerato nella stessa tabella azzerava le coordinate di ogni riga (27 titoli irraggiungibili su una sola serie) e gli extra numerati oltre la serie regolare non venivano più trovati. Timeout della traduzione portato a 90 secondi: il tetto di 30 tagliava richieste sane.

v0.4.5.0: rilascio di correzioni, tre difetti trovati provando il plugin su una libreria reale. Le sinossi italiane da TheTVDB non hanno mai funzionato: la pagina episodi veniva scartata per una forma di risposta assunta male, e su otto serie di prova TheTVDB aveva 119 sinossi italiane su 212 episodi, tutte irraggiungibili. Le sinossi di AnimeClick mancavano su ogni episodio con un accento nel titolo, perché l'identificativo salvato veniva rifiutato dal plugin stesso: il 13% degli episodi in prova. Una stagione intera poteva ricevere i titoli sfalsati di una posizione quando la tabella di AnimeClick contiene più righe di quante ne dichiari: ora la discordanza viene rilevata e serve la conferma del titolo del file, altrimenti l'episodio resta intatto. Inoltre: i titoli che ripetono solo il numero non vengono più scritti, la coda delle traduzioni non può più fermarsi in silenzio, e verso TheTVDB, TMDB e AniList c'è un passo minimo con rispetto delle richieste di rallentamento.

v0.4.4.0: audit del codice in tre giri, senza nuove funzionalità. Correttezza: le righe “Speciale” non diventano più episodi numerati con l'anno (prima spostavano la numerazione degli episodi successivi o rompevano la divisione automatica in stagioni), e il filtro sulle locandine a bassa risoluzione non si disattiva più da solo. Sicurezza: allow-list host HTTPS su tutti gli URL immagine (serie, film, episodi, stagioni e anteprime di ricerca), tetto di 15 minuti al Retry-After del server per non bloccare lo scraping fino al riavvio, impostazioni validate sul server e non solo nella pagina di configurazione. Robustezza: timeout e limiti di dimensione su tutte le chiamate di rete, budget sul recupero della lista episodi di TheTVDB, token TheTVDB scartato quando viene rifiutato invece di essere riusato per 24 ore, errori di chiave API e di rete ora visibili nel log invece che solo a livello Debug, un errore di scrittura della cache non fa più perdere i metadati dell'elemento, e cache per le foto degli autori.

v0.4.3.0: voce del plugin nella sidebar del pannello di controllo; banner del footer mostrato per intero; fix SSRF sugli URL immagine di serie/film (allow-list host HTTPS); HttpClient via IHttpClientFactory per evitare collisioni tra versioni; rimozione di memory leak nei lock, pulizia dello stato più efficiente e parsing/regex indipendenti dal locale; modello Ollama Cloud predefinito ora gpt-oss:20b-cloud con migrazione automatica.

v0.4.2.0: AnimeClick diventa la prima fonte per le sinossi degli episodi, ignorando descrizioni vuote, segnaposto e commenti; fallback TheTVDB/TMDB/Ollama, matching indipendente dai titoli, cache e diagnostica aggiornate; README riscritto per l'utente finale.

v0.4.1.0: Resolver episodi/stagioni v5 fail-safe con layout multipli, separazione tra episodi regolari e speciali, override deterministici e cache single-flight; diagnostica e frontend aggiornati con banner/footer; documentazione Ollama EN→IT ampliata.

v0.4.0.0: AnimeClick-first con authority layer lock-aware, resolver stagioni v4, metadati semantici estesi, coda asincrona Ollama con backoff e cache content-addressed, e fix E14-E26 per stagioni sintetiche.

v0.3.8.0: Fortificazione e ottimizzazione ricerca metadata. Filtro qualità immagini: MinPosterWidth (default 400px, ora in UI) — se AnimeClick fornisce locandina (o artwork) a bassa risoluzione viene automaticamente saltata e Jellyfin passa ad altri provider configurati (Fanart/AniList/TMDB). Probe efficiente con HTTP Range + cache. Search: cleaners robusti (sequel, fullwidth, &), scorer fuzzy migliorato, retry transienti nel client. Bugfix: versioning assembly corretto, UA dinamico, TvdbLanguage sanitizzato, Person images Order=100. Aggiornamenti UI e docs.

v0.3.7.0: Fix multi-stagione quando AnimeClick elenca episodi in blocco unico (es. The Asterisk War 24ep/2cour). Parser sintetizza SeasonNumber da <dt>Stagioni</dt> main-page. Matches S2 via seasonOrdinal.

v0.3.6.0: Fix TVDB tvdb_id restituito come stringa (API v4 /search) + fallback al campo id. Gestione accenti italiani in ricerca AnimeClick (RemoveDiacritics su query e scorer). Timeout 30s su IdentifyAndRefresh con risposta graceful. Ollama ParseTranslatedContent gestisce \uXXXX e surrogate pairs. Attribution TheTVDB (banner config + README).
v0.3.5.0: Fix TVDB search (type=series filter broken in v4 API, filter client-side).

v0.3.4.0: Fix HTTP 415 sui pulsanti Test TMDB/Ollama/TVDB e Svuota cache. I POST dal frontend venivano inviati senza body e senza Content-Type, causando 415 da ASP.NET Core prima di contattare le API esterne.
v0.3.3.0: Update logo to gatto.png and change title to AnimeClick Plugin

v0.3.2.0: Remake completo del frontend con architettura modulare in stile KometaThemes. CSS esterno (ac- design system, palette arancione), JS esterno (form dinamici, dirty-state, toast, modal), HTML bootstrapper minimale. Quattro tab (Overview, Metadati, Sinossi, Strumenti), hero con stat tile, sticky save bar, feature chips, provider test con live dot. Ogni impostazione mappata 1:1 al backend.

v0.3.1.0: Fix download immagini. GetImageResponse ora invia User-Agent/Referer (il CDN AnimeClick rifiutava le richieste senza UA → HTTP 403, locandine e foto staff non scaricate). Nuova opzione MinPosterWidth: scarta le locandine sotto la risoluzione minima e passa al provider successivo (Fanart/TMDB/AniList).

v0.3.0.0: Redesign completo del frontend — premium dashboard UI. Nuova interfaccia glassmorphism con gradienti animati, tipografia premium, micro-interazioni fluide, nuovi bottoni e badge. UX/UI migliorata con card più eleganti e layout rivisitato.

v0.2.11: Nuova dashboard premium glassmorphism con header sticky, tab bar iconata a pillole, tile stato provider, azioni rapide e save dock fisso. Ricerca impostazioni live e descrizioni toggleabili. Backend invariato.

v0.2.9: TheTVDB come fonte preferita per le sinossi degli episodi in italiano, con traduzione diretta e zero carico sul NAS. Se TVDB non ha la traduzione, il plugin usa il fallback TMDB piu Ollama Cloud. Aggiunti i pulsanti di test TMDB, Ollama e TVDB per verificare le credenziali inserite con messaggi di errore dettagliati.

v0.2.10: Pagina di configurazione rinnovata. Quattro schede in alto (Metadati, Sinossi episodi, Ricerca, Strumenti) con card visive e icone. Rimossa la sezione diagnostica tecnica, sostituita da strumenti piu semplici: Identifica e Aggiorna, e Svuota cache con un clic. I test di connessione TMDB, Ollama e TVDB ora mostrano un badge Connesso o Errore invece del testo tecnico. Risolto il bug dei pulsanti di test che mostravano parentesi vuote.

v0.2.8: AnimeClick ora fornisce solo i campi in italiano (titolo, trama, generi, tag, cast) e lascia agli altri provider i campi neutri come studio, anno e valutazione. Aggiunta la locandina italiana di AnimeClick come immagine di fallback quando AniList, Fanart o TMDB non hanno immagini. Sinossi degli episodi in italiano opzionali via TMDB piu Ollama Cloud.

v0.2.7: AniList ID risolto durante OGNI scan, non solo nell'Identify manuale. Nuovo servizio AnimeClickAniListResolver (estratto da AnimeClickIdentifyController, registrato in DI, DRY). SeriesProvider e MovieProvider ora risolvono e scrivono ProviderIds[AniList] in GetMetadata a ogni scansione, usando il titolo originale (romaji) con fallback al titolo italiano: le pagine AnimeClick non espongono link MAL/AniList/AniDB/TMDB, quindi questo fallback e cio che permette all'ImageFetcher AniList di scaricare le copertine in automatico e fornisce ai provider a valle un ID stabile. Nota: Fanart per i film usa il TMDB ID, quindi abilita anche TheMovieDb come metadata fetcher nella libreria Anime Movie. Controller rifattorizzato per riusare il servizio + nuovi unit test su parsing JSON ed escaping GraphQL.

v0.2.6: Fix response body undefined (client JS leggeva PascalCase, ASP.NET Core serializza in camelCase) + fix RemoteImageQuery che passava providerName=string.Empty (filtrava per provider con nome vuoto, ritornando array vuoto per Primary/Backdrop/Logo/Art/Thumb). v0.2.6.0 usa providerName: null (tutti i provider) + IncludeDisabledProviders=true. Nuovo EnsureAniListIdAsync che interroga AniList GraphQL per titolo e salva l'AniList ID sull'item prima del download immagini (necessario perché AnimeClick non fornisce TMDB/IMDB/AniList ID, quindi senza AniList ID l'AniList ImageFetcher non può fare lookup). DownloadedImages list ora visualizzata in modo leggibile nel result box della configPage.

versions.changelog: v1.4.1.0: Replaces the generic comet mark with an original anime mascot across every plugin page, the item action, Jellyfin's dashboard sidebar, GitHub and the plugin catalog. Rewrites the README around installation, first-time setup and everyday workflows, and corrects outdated interface-language and YouTube extractor requirements. Release build with no warnings, 221 unit tests and 14 browser and accessibility tests. No breaking changes.

v1.4.0.0: YouTube import no longer needs anything installed. The extractor now travels inside the plugin package, so pasting a link works on a stock Jellyfin server; previously the feature reported that yt-dlp was missing and did nothing until somebody installed it by hand inside the container, where it also disappeared on the next container update. yt-dlp is still supported and is still preferred automatically when present, with no configuration, because it tracks YouTube's changes continuously while a bundled copy only moves when this plugin is released; neither is required, and the settings page reports which of the two is in use. Video is assembled from a container-matched video and audio pair rather than taken from one of YouTube's pre-muxed streams, which top out at 360p; the join is a stream copy, so it costs no re-encode, measured against real YouTube at 1080p VP9 plus Opus with 0.9s to download and 5.2s to join. Packaging note: the archive now contains four assemblies instead of one — the plugin plus YoutubeExplode, AngleSharp and JsonExtensions. Install through the plugin catalog as usual, Jellyfin unpacks all of them. The archive is packed from an explicit list rather than from the build output folder, which also holds around thirty Jellyfin and Microsoft.Extensions assemblies that must not ship, and the build fails if that set ever changes. Release build with no warnings, 220 unit tests and 14 browser tests. No breaking changes.

v1.2.0.0: The YouTube import introduced in 1.1.0.0 had only been verified with unit tests, a mocked interface and a successful build. Running it against real yt-dlp and ffmpeg surfaced three problems, one of them serious: the video path forced the webm container, so every source YouTube serves as H.264 was re-encoded to VP9 before it could be written. Measured on four cores at roughly a quarter of realtime: 76 seconds for a 20-second 1080p clip, which is about 13 minutes of pegged CPU for a single three-and-a-half-minute theme, and worse on NAS hardware. Jellyfin accepts any video it can recognise inside backdrops, so the webm constraint was never its own; it came from animethemes.moe having been the only source. The source container is now carried through and the stream simply copied, and the same video takes 7 seconds. Also fixed: a theme video with no video track is rejected instead of being written as a silent, picture-less backdrop, and theme videos are recognised in both webm and mp4 everywhere, including the link repair that registers them with Jellyfin (an imported mp4 previously existed on disk and never played). Configuration: ten places mutated the shared object without synchronization, so two dashboard actions at the same time could lose one of the two entries or fail part-way through writing the file; they all go through a single lock now. Seasons: a later season is no longer confidently given an earlier season's themes, because the group number was a position over episode ranges rather than a season the source declared, and a miss fell back to the first group; ordinals are now trusted only when the ranges divide the run cleanly, and otherwise all themes are offered. A single-season show no longer gets the same opening written twice, into both the series folder and the season folder. Growth and contention: the skip list, the manual bindings, the resolution cache and the unresolved list were all unbounded, and cache entries expired only if something queried that exact key again; all of them are capped now and the cache is swept on a schedule, and reads of the two stores no longer block a thread each. Also: stale theme references are removed instead of accumulating, a malformed library pattern can no longer hang a sync, the playlist is written atomically and removed when empty, ffmpeg runs are capped plugin-wide (the previous limit applied only within a single request), and the choice of the root theme.mp3 is deterministic. 213 unit tests and 15 interface and accessibility tests. No breaking changes.

v1.3.1.0: The Theme Finder no longer shows a message about yt-dlp. Opening it on a server without the extractor produced an error-styled panel reading "yt-dlp was not found. Install it in the Jellyfin environment, or set its full path in the plugin settings.", in the middle of the page you opened to add a theme; an install instruction for a command-line tool is not an answer to that intent, and it made a feature that was never enabled look broken. When YouTube import is turned off, or the extractor is not installed, the import card is simply not shown. Whether the extractor was found, and where it was searched for, is still reported on the plugin settings page, directly below the YouTube import toggle and the yt-dlp path field, which is where it is actionable. Release build with no warnings, 213 unit tests and 13 browser tests; two new tests assert the card is absent, one for a missing extractor and one for the feature being off, and check that the string yt-dlp appears nowhere in the page. No breaking changes.

v1.3.0.0: The plugin interface is English only. The Italian translation and the interface-language setting in the General tab have been removed, along with the language machinery behind them: each page now ships one string table instead of two, and a missing string shows its key rather than rendering blank. Existing configurations keep working — the stored language value is simply ignored, so no settings are lost on upgrade. Italian season names are deliberately still recognised: "2ª Stagione", "2° Stagione" and "stagione 2" continue to resolve to season 2, because those are folder and series names read from your library rather than interface text, and dropping them would have silently broken season detection for Italian-named libraries. Release build with no warnings, 213 unit tests and 12 interface and accessibility tests; the browser count is down from 15 because the axe audit no longer runs every page twice, once per language. No breaking changes.

v1.1.0.0: New — openings and endings that animethemes.moe does not have can now be added by pasting a YouTube link into the Theme Finder: you are asked whether it is an OP or an ED, and whether you want audio, video or both. The feature is off by default and needs yt-dlp installed in the Jellyfin environment; the settings page reports whether it was found. Important data-loss fixes: an interrupted conversion no longer leaves a corrupt theme file that every later sync skipped as "already downloaded", with no sync or force sync able to repair it; deleting an item no longer wipes the theme-music and backdrops folders wholesale, which in a flat library destroyed every other item's themes and the user's own fanart; a force sync no longer deletes files it did not create, including those added through the Theme Finder; the cache and the unresolved list survive an abrupt shutdown. Themes whose download failed now stay in the Unresolved list instead of silently disappearing, and cancelling a sync leaves a finished state instead of a stuck progress bar. Also fixed: large theme videos are no longer cut off after 30 seconds, one provider erroring no longer stops resolution for the whole library, libraries with more than 100 items are no longer partly ignored, sequels and later seasons are no longer confidently bound to the wrong entry, and the playlist also finds items in subfolders. Interface: the ♪ button no longer polls the server every 1.5 seconds, keyboard use in the Theme Finder no longer selects the audio when triggering the preview or the video, and themes chosen across several seasons are attributed to the correct anime. No breaking changes.

v1.0.8.0: New unified high-contrast brand icon (comet plus musical note), shown consistently across every plugin page, the Theme Finder action and the Jellyfin dashboard sidebar. The icon is now a single embedded SVG asset instead of duplicated inline copies, and the sidebar entry no longer shows the generic folder. No breaking changes.

v1.0.7.1: Fixed secondary text contrast, with a stable WCAG AA margin that holds in CI renderers too. Stabilised the Playwright and axe audits by waiting for the asynchronous cache data and excluding in-flight animations. No breaking changes.

v1.0.7.0: Shared fail-closed frontend loader, reusable accessibility primitives, improved WCAG contrast and form fields, and corrected Theme Finder bulk actions. New Playwright suite with 13 end-to-end and axe tests. Full README with a language selector and official Buy Me a Coffee, PayPal and GitHub buttons. No breaking changes.

v1.0.6.0: Frontend remake and shared hardening across the configuration page, the Theme Finder and the item page. New keyboard tab navigation, accessible modals with a focus trap, live regions, responsive layout and busy states. Fixes for stale async responses, double submissions, the Audio/Video filters and bulk selection, remote URLs and sanitised API messages. No breaking changes.
v1.0.5.1: Further centralize ForceSync (explicit param), theme rows keyboard, SVG logo polish, more UI/harden.
v1.0.5.0: ForceSync centralization (explicit bool force param). Theme row keyboard support + SVG logo polish. Further UI/ARIA, harden, tests. Eligibility audit.
v1.0.4.1: Refined IsItemEligible (better detection for edge cases like 'Belle'). Eligibility errors now translated when UiLanguage=Italian. Bug fixes for false 'not in library' on valid anime.
v1.0.4.0: Harden (no live config mutation, explicit force). Bug fixes for sync/non-anime. UI: keyboard for broad results + clearer labels.

v1.0.3.1: Fixed Sync now / Force sync buttons (Sync now is now always incremental, ignores ForceSync checkbox). Prevented scanning non-anime folders in auto-sync, single-item sync and playlist. Eligibility gates added. No more unnecessary redownloads on normal sync.

v1.0.3.0: LibraryPattern now gates ♪ button + item UI (non-anime fix). IsItemEligible + /eligible + guards. Theme Finder: keyboard nav (arrows/Home/End/Enter/Esc), clear button, ARIA (listbox/activedescendant), strong focus/active/hover visuals. All prior harden + filters included. Version per AGENTS.

v1.0.2.0: Completed Theme Finder quick filters (Audio/Video, OP/ED, Creditless only) with 'Select visible' and clear. Per-season group bulk select buttons. Full active filter state. Parser hardening + new tests. Config bounds enforcement (NormalizeBounds). Auth policies standardized to Policies.RequiresElevation. UI polish and responsive updates. Version bump per AGENTS.md.
