versions.changelog: Fixes the friends list showing "Failed to load friends" for anyone who actually had friends (issue #79). The list was loading correctly - it crashed while drawing the first friend, and that crash was being reported as a loading failure. A user with no friends never hit it, which is why it took a report to find. The panel now explains what went wrong instead of showing one generic line, offers a Retry, and is translated in every language. In media management you can also choose which copy of a duplicate to keep (issue #80) - press Keep this on any copy and the bin moves to the others, which matters when identical copies sit on different drives.

Finishes the translation work and adds a security pass. An audit of the whole plugin found another 141 phrases written straight into the markup - the profile settings window, the rating box, review comments, the media picker and its sort menu, friend menus, chat controls, moderator and ban dialogs, and every "nothing here yet" message. All of them are translated now, in all fifteen languages, and each pack carries around 560 phrases where it had about 348. On security: no exploitable weakness was found, and three things were tightened. Profile header uploads now check the file really is a GIF, MP4 or WEBM rather than trusting its name, since the address serving them is public by design. Bug report screenshots are fetched with your access token in a header instead of the web address, keeping it out of browser history. And asking for better quality now respects each account's library access. The dashboard heading also shows the right version again.

The profile page, the friends panel and the star rating widget are translated at last. Those three areas were never connected to the translation system - the words were written straight into the markup - so they stayed in English no matter which language you picked, in all sixteen languages. Forty-seven labels now go through the translation layer and are filled in for every language: the friends panel and its tabs, the profile tab strip and stat row, follow, block and friend buttons, the rating popup, and the whole sidebar down to Stats, Films, Shows, Hours, Taste, Similar Taste, Add a film, Back, Member since and the "not on server" badge. The thirty-eight strings from the quality-request and bug-report queues are translated too. Every language pack gains eighty-five entries. Thanks to chosqui for reporting it in discussion #76 with a Spanish patch that showed exactly what was missing.

Three fixes to the support queues added last release, all found by using them on a real server. The Quality and Bug Reports tabs never appeared in the Request Media window: that window is built in more than one place in the client and only one of them had been given the new tabs, so the two queues had no way in. Opening a request or a report drew the detail window underneath the one it was launched from, which made clicking a Quality row look as though nothing happened at all. And people who sent a bug report had no way of telling whether anyone had looked at it - the report box now lists your own reports beneath it with their status and any reply, and sending one no longer closes the window, so the report lands in that list in front of you. Note: after updating, reload the page with the cache cleared. The browser holds on to the page that references the previous version of the plugin's script, and until it lets go you will still be running the old one.

Two new ways for people to tell you something is wrong, and one place to work through both. A Better Quality tab on the profile searches what is already on the server, and every result carries a button to say what is wrong with the current copy - blurry, wrong audio, missing subtitles. A Report a problem button next to Edit Profile takes a description plus screenshots, pasted straight from the clipboard or picked from disk. Both land in the Request Media window as their own tabs, badged with how many are still open, where you can read the report, look at the screenshots, reply to the person who sent it, and mark it solved or declined - your reply is shown back to them. This release also fixes a profile showing 0 films and 0 hours next to a taste chart reporting hundreds of hours: those figures came from ratings alone, so anyone who watches without rating saw zeros. They now count what you have watched as well as what you have rated. And the genre breakdown was the one part of a profile with no privacy check, so a private profile's viewing habits could be read by anyone signed in.

The request list in the admin panel now lays out properly on a phone. Each request kept its title, user, date and status on a single row, so on a narrow screen the title was squeezed down to a few characters, and the media-link and rejection-reason boxes were split across a width that could not hold them. The title now takes a line of its own with the details underneath it, the expand arrow sits at the right edge, and the two input boxes stack at full width. Reported and written by @daki456. The input rules also apply in every language now - they previously keyed off the English placeholder text, so they did nothing on a translated server.

Fixes the request list in the admin panel. A category holding more requests than fit on screen squashed its cards down into unreadable slivers instead of scrolling - the cards were being compressed to fit the available height rather than keeping their own. Each category now scrolls once it passes 500 pixels, with the cards at their normal size. Thanks to @daki456 for reporting and fixing it.

Leftover trickplay cleanup now covers both ways Jellyfin stores it. Libraries set to 'save trickplay images next to media' keep the tiles in a folder beside each video rather than in the central directory, and those were invisible to the previous scan - a server using that setting appeared to have no trickplay at all. Both places are now scanned and cleaned, and the panel reports what it found in each. Verified on a live library: it correctly identified real leftovers from deleted media while leaving every folder whose video is still present untouched.

Fixes the leftover-trickplay cleanup, which previously reported nothing to clean up on every server. Jellyfin stores trickplay in folders grouped by the first two characters of each item id, and the scan was treating one of those groups as the whole directory - so it looked at a single group out of 256, usually an empty one. It now reads the real directory and looks inside every group. The panel also showed internal labels instead of readable text, and now names the directory it checked and how many folders it examined, so 'nothing to clean up' can be told apart from a scan that never ran.

Two clean-ups from the security review. Searching and browsing through the plugin now respects the libraries each account is allowed to see, so a user with limited access can no longer come across titles from libraries they cannot open - this affected the plugin's own search, the sorted library view and the latest-media list. Playback was never affected. And when the plugin refuses an action because you are not an administrator, it now says so properly instead of returning a server error; access was already correctly denied, but the message was wrong. Privacy defaults are unchanged - profiles remain visible to everyone unless the user chooses otherwise.

Security and features. Fixes three ways a user could have got script to run inside someone else's session: one through a profile's favourite films, which affected anyone viewing that profile, and two through links attached to media and deletion requests, which ran in an administrator's session. Also closes several privacy and permission gaps - private profiles could be read through the newer profile endpoints, a private list could be read by copying it, direct messages ignored blocking, the recent-requests list showed every user's requests to non-administrators, and a user banned from playback or over quota could bypass both by sending their login token in a different but equally valid form. New: leftover trickplay data can now be cleared from Media Management, so space used by tiles belonging to deleted media can be recovered without reprocessing everything you still have. Search now ignores punctuation and spacing, so 'xfiles', 'x files' and 'X-Files' all find the same show. Ratings can be edited or removed from the Ratings tab, including titles not on the server; reviews can be written for those titles; custom profile rows can be reordered; and any rating can be agreed or disagreed with, not only ones with a written review. The Reviews tab now shows posters. Fixes the empty gap under the header on phones, the plugin's buttons covering the video player in portrait, and missing posters in Recent Activity. Every endpoint now identifies you the same way, so apps signing in with a plain token are no longer refused.

Profile favourites and Media Management fixes. Adding a title from the catalog to a favourites row now works and stays: the button no longer ignores films whose name contains an apostrophe, the card is no longer discarded when you reopen the profile, and rows containing only catalog titles now show them straight away instead of only after adding something else. Titles lost by the earlier fault need re-adding once. Media Management was showing no posters, no media type and dashes for rating, plays, size and status - it now reads every field correctly, and the same fault is fixed on the Scheduled tab, the 'Leaving in' badges, and the media request and ban screens. Media that Jellyfin has not identified, which has no artwork at all, now falls back to a poster from TMDB where one can be found. On phones the header menu is now a compact row of icons rather than one full-width row per button, which previously left most buttons unreachable, plus a layout fix for the ElegantFin skin that is applied only on servers actually using it.

Fixes rating a film that is not on the server failing with a not-authenticated error. Four endpoints checked the signed-in user in a stricter way than the rest of the plugin and rejected perfectly valid requests - rating a TMDB title, reading your own rating for an item, the batch rating lookup used to draw badges, and listing or creating media requests. They now identify you the same way every other endpoint does, so any client sending a valid token is accepted.

Fixes new media being announced but never appearing in the Latest Media list. The list was ordered by the date Jellyfin takes from the file itself, not by when the media actually reached your server - so anything copied in keeping its original timestamps sorted to wherever that old date fell, usually past the end of the list. You would get the 'now available' notification and then find nothing there. The list now also includes everything the plugin announced, dated by when it actually saw it, so the notification and the list can no longer disagree. Items removed from the server since being announced are left out.

Further hardening of the watching hover card, following up the security fix in the previous version. The card no longer reads any text back out of the page at all - the title it shows while loading now comes from data the plugin already holds. Re-inserting text taken from the page undoes whatever escaping made it safe, so the read was removed rather than escaped. Numbers shown on the card (year, running time, score) are also validated as numbers before being displayed, which additionally stops an unexpected value breaking the card.

Security fix. The hover card that shows what someone is watching built an image tag by pasting an item id straight into HTML, and that id was read back out of the page. A crafted value could have escaped the image tag and run script for another user viewing the profile. Item ids are now rejected unless they are genuine Jellyfin ids, and the image is created as a real element instead of being assembled from text, so nothing untrusted can reach the markup. Reported by GitHub CodeQL (js/xss-through-dom, high severity).

API fixes for third-party and TV clients. Social endpoints previously accepted only the raw X-Emby-Token header, so any app using Jellyfin's standard authentication got 401 from every social call while the identical request worked against the ratings API - they now accept every form Jellyfin does, including API keys. All responses are also camelCase now; some endpoints returned PascalCase and others camelCase, which silently produced empty fields in other clients. Your existing data is unaffected. New endpoints make a profile page far cheaper to build: one aggregated profile call instead of nine, ratings/reviews/activity that already include title, poster and year, a per-user rating histogram, a capability check, and paging on followers and following. Nothing changes in the web interface.

Hover what someone is watching to see the poster and details. Pointing at the title in the Similar Taste list now brings up a card with the artwork, year, running time, age rating, community score, genres and a synopsis - so you can tell what it is without leaving the profile. For an episode it shows the series artwork and the episode name. Details are fetched once and remembered for the rest of the session.

Live presence, full titles, and a Watch too button. The Similar Taste list now updates by itself when someone comes online or starts watching - you no longer have to close and reopen the profile to see it. What someone is watching moved onto its own line, so long series titles are readable in full instead of being squeezed between the name and the match percentage. And each person who is watching now has a Watch too button: press it and you are asked whether to join them at the point they are at right now, or start from the beginning.

See who is online and what they are watching, and a much better looking profile name. The Similar Taste list now shows a dot on each person: bright green and pulsing means they are watching something right now, and the card shows what it is with a clock that ticks along live; soft green means online but not watching; grey means offline. The profile name has also been fixed - it was drawn as a colour gradient clipped to the letters, which over a photo or video header turned it into washed-out grey. It is now solid white with proper display typography, using each platform's large-text typeface.

See what you actually watch, find people with the same taste, and Back now works properly. Profiles have a new Taste ring in the sidebar showing your genre breakdown by real watch time - taken from what you have actually played, not just what you rated - with total hours and a percentage per genre. Below it, a Similar Taste list ranks everyone on the server by how closely their genre mix matches yours, showing the genres you have most in common; click anyone to open their profile, or use the envelope button to message them directly. Also fixed: opening someone's profile from a followers or match list and pressing Back used to close the whole profile window instead of returning to the profile you came from.

Rate films that are not on the server, keep ratings readable after media is deleted, choose your TMDB search language, and browse other users. You can now rate a title added to a profile row from the catalog even though it is not on the server - hover it and press Rate. If it is added to the library later, your rating attaches to it automatically. Ratings also remember the title, year and poster of what you rated, so deleting a film no longer leaves a nameless row of stars behind; older ratings fill this in as you use them. Admins can set the language TMDB search returns titles in (Settings, TMDB Search Language) instead of always getting English. And profiles have a new Other Users tab listing everyone on the server, with a filter box, so you can find and visit other people's profiles without knowing their name in advance.

Header buttons now fold into a dropdown menu on phones. With search, language, profile, requests, notifications, latest media, chat and friends all in the header there was simply not enough room on a small screen, and buttons ended up clipped or wrapping badly. On phone-sized screens they now sit behind a single arrow button and open as a tidy list, with the search box at full width. Unread chat messages light a dot on that button so you can still tell something is waiting inside. Nothing changes on tablets or desktop. Thanks to @chosqui for the suggestion (discussion #71).

Fixes from reported issues. The Save button in Profile Settings now works - it was calling an address the server does not accept, so nothing was ever saved, and the privacy tick-boxes always looked switched on regardless of your real settings (#72). The search bar no longer disappears on phones held in portrait: it shrinks to just the magnifier icon and expands when tapped, instead of being hidden on any screen under 400px wide (#69). Deleting media now also removes its trickplay thumbnails and any extracted subtitles or attachments, which used to be left behind forever (#70). Uninstalling the plugin now really removes the header buttons - the plugin no longer edits Jellyfin's index.html, and it cleans up that edit if an older version made one, so users no longer have to clear their browser cache by hand (#66). When an old plugin folder cannot be deleted on Windows because its file is locked, the plugin now removes that folder's meta.json so the stale version stops being listed and loaded (#67). New-media notifications now log why an item was treated as new, to make the remaining reports diagnosable (#65).

Much smaller downloads and far less disk activity. The plugin's script, stylesheet and language files are now sent pre-compressed, so a first page load transfers roughly 108 KB instead of 676 KB - about six times less. This applies even if you reach Jellyfin over HTTPS directly, where Jellyfin's own compression is off by default. Separately, rapid saves are now merged into a single write: previously every user's presence heartbeat rewrote the entire online-users file, so a few people online meant constant disk churn. Nothing is lost - pending saves are flushed on shutdown and before any backup export or import.

Big speed and smoothness pass. Pages load about a third lighter: the plugin's styles are now a proper stylesheet instead of being stuffed inside the script, and only your own language is downloaded rather than all sixteen. Scrolling through libraries is noticeably smoother because the plugin no longer re-scans the whole page every time anything on it changes. The admin Media list now asks the database for just the page you're looking at instead of loading your entire library first, so it opens quickly even on large collections. Chat only fetches new messages instead of re-downloading the last 50 every two seconds, and background tabs stop polling entirely. Watching something no longer rewrites a settings file every few seconds of playback. Data files are also written more safely, so a crash or power cut mid-save can no longer leave them corrupted. Includes the admin category list scrollbar fix from PR #73.

Properly fixes the 'new media' pop-ups that kept appearing for films and shows already on your server. The plugin now learns your whole existing library the first time it runs and only alerts you about genuinely new additions. A library scan, a re-scan, or installing the plugin on a big existing collection no longer floods you with 'now available' alerts for old content - including whole seasons that were already there. Re-scans and re-added files no longer fool it either.

Your ratings now live in Jellyfin too, plus a compatibility fix. Every rating you give is also saved into Jellyfin's own rating, so other apps and tools (like Maintainerr) can find and use your ratings. A one-time 'Sync existing ratings to Jellyfin' button in the plugin settings copies all your past ratings across in one click; new ratings are saved automatically. There's also an optional setting to write the average score into each item's Community Rating (off by default - it replaces the existing IMDb/TMDB score and is undone when Jellyfin refreshes metadata). Fix: the Friends panel (Online tab, friend search) and live chat no longer throw errors on the latest Jellyfin (10.11.10/10.11.11).

Big profile update plus speed and fixes. Faster Latest Media and browsing on large libraries. Hover the rating stars to see the number inside the star. New admin option to show/hide the rating badge on poster cards. Add films/shows that are NOT on the server to your profile rows - drag them in from search or Recent Activity, hover for a Request button. Drag any search result (on-server or catalog) straight into a row. Hover any poster or search result to see its full title, year and description. Upload your own looping GIF or video to show behind your profile name and picture. Fixes: deleting a duplicate now really removes the file (no more reappearing), the rating number no longer sticks after you move off a star, header text stays readable over a video background, and dragging from Recent Activity now reliably sticks.

Speed and reliability improvements. Made the 'Latest Media' panel and general browsing noticeably faster on large libraries by removing heavy background work that ran every minute. Fixed old movies and shows sometimes appearing as 'newly added' when they were not - now only genuinely new media triggers a notification, and the same item is never announced twice (even after a server restart). Fixed custom sorting showing no cards when several folders are combined into one library view.

Faster loading and a duplicate-finder fix. Pages now open quicker: the plugin's add-on is cached by your browser and packaged about a third smaller, so it doesn't re-download every time. Also fixed the Duplicates tool wrongly flagging whole TV shows as duplicates (it was treating every episode of a series as a copy) - it now only groups true duplicates.
Security and cleanup: removed an old, unused profile page that triggered security warnings. The profile you actually use and all other features are unchanged.

Big profile update. Build your profile your way with favorite rows you can name, drag to reorder, and drag posters straight from your recent activity. Search any film or show — watch it if it's on the server, or request it in one click if it isn't. Your ratings, reviews and activity now show the real titles, and you can like or dislike reviews. Faster loading, a cleaner look with a background picker, and lots of fixes including favorites that now save reliably.

My Rating library sort fixed (owned grid - no more page 2/3 reset or empty results), unified API auth, performance (cached ratings.js + parallel data load), auto-removal of duplicate plugin folders, and a redesigned Letterboxd-style profile: real media names everywhere, exact-rating tooltips, clickable media to watch, 'Add a film' search/request, two-column layout with right sidebar, poster reflections, animations and a background picker.

versions.changelog: v1.8.3.30: notifications stack instead of piling up - issue #77, 'if you hit a toggle in quick succession, the notifications at the lower right side of the screen will simply pile on top of each other'. They did, literally: every notification was its own position:fixed element anchored to the same corner, so two of them resolved to the identical coordinates and the second covered the first. Measured in a browser against the real CSS - three toasts all reported top 1185 / bottom 1226; after the fix 1185, 1136, 1087 with no overlap. They are flow children of one fixed host now and the host does the stacking, column-reverse so the newest sits nearest the corner. Two things beyond the literal report, both aimed at what 'quick succession' actually produces: a repeated toggle emits the SAME text over and over, so an identical message already on screen has its timer restarted instead of being cloned (firing 'Settings saved!' five times leaves one), and the stack is capped at four so holding a control down cannot fill the viewport. THE PLUGIN HAD THREE COPIES of this code, each with the same defect - the config page (reported), the player overlay and the quick menu - and all three are fixed, because patching only the reported surface is how the same bug gets filed twice. sidebar-upscaler.js was already correct (it defers to Jellyfin's own toast module) and a test now keeps it that way. Verified by measurement, not by reading: a browser harness built from the real CSS and the real showToast confirmed stacking, de-duplication and the cap, and re-applying the old position:fixed rule reproduced the exact overlap from the screenshot. Eleven regression tests; five reintroduced defects are each caught. 375 C# + 166 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.29: the error message now says what went wrong. Testing v1.8.3.28 live showed the last piece of the same problem - a failed Load Detection Model printed one generic sentence regardless of cause, because the handler read err.responseText (an XHR field) while Jellyfin 10.11's client is fetch-based. Checked against the running server rather than assumed: the rejection is [object Response], err.text IS a function, err.responseText does not exist, status 404 - so JSON.parse(undefined) threw on every failure and the fallback was the only thing anyone saw, while the body carried exactly what was needed ('... is not on disk. Import or upload a detection model first'). That reaches the status line now. The same run confirmed the v1.8.3.28 modelName parameter end to end: the service named the id that was passed, not the saved one. The old fallback also advised saving the settings first, which stopped being true in v1.8.3.28 when the button began saving them itself. 364 C# + 166 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.28: the two object-masking UI bugs reported in discussion #11, where the feature itself is confirmed working - Ultralytics YOLO exports load (YOLO26n fastest in the reporter's testing), boxes land where they should, 5-10 fps at low quality on a Ryzen 5 7600 through docker7-cpu. 'THE STATUS WOULD OFTEN STICK ON A PREVIOUS MODEL NAME' - because it was telling the truth: the button POSTed nothing and the endpoint read only the SAVED config, so a newly typed id loaded the PREVIOUS model and the status correctly named that one. A comment in the UI described this exact trap and guarded only against an empty field; documenting a bug is not fixing it. The endpoint takes a modelName parameter now, the button sends what is on screen, and the saved value stays as the fallback for scripts. 'IT SEEMED TO IGNORE THE CONFIDENCE VALUES I PUT IN' - it did. step=0.05 makes a type=number input report value === '' for entries the browser rejects, and floating point puts ordinary values off that grid: (0.6-0.05)/0.05 evaluates to 10.999999999999998, so 0.6 was rejected. The save path skipped empty strings, which normally means 'left blank' but here meant 'the browser disliked it', so the number vanished without a word. Now step=any, parsed and clamped, and the stored value written back into the field. Both share a root cause: an action button sits next to fields that were not persisted until the global Save, so Load Detection Model now saves the card first - which also stops values reverting when you navigate away and back. Four regression tests, each verified to fail when its fix is reverted. 364 C# + 166 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.27: three defects a live server showed that no unit test could. EVERY TRANSLATED STRING HAS BEEN FALLING BACK TO ITS KEY on every install since the i18n work landed - strings.en.json is declared as an EmbeddedResource, MSBuild lists it as one, and it was not in the DLL, because MSBuild reads the '.en.' in the file name as a CULTURE TAG and compiles it into a satellite assembly the release ZIP does not ship. Jellyfin logged 'Failed to get resource' on every config-page load. The test guarding it asserted that the .csproj MENTIONED the file, which it always did; it now reads the built assembly's manifest resource names, and removing the fix fails it. /hardware-info REPORTED THREE THINGS IT NEVER CHECKED: GpuAvailable returned the HardwareAcceleration config toggle (default on), so a CPU-only server was told it had a GPU while /gpu-verify on the same box reported no devices at all; FFmpegAvailable was the literal true and OnnxRuntime the literal 'Available'. All three are observations now, null means 'not asked yet' rather than 'no', and what the user requested is a separate field. THE FRAME PROXIES THREW AWAY THE DIAGNOSIS: after a container restart the service answers {'detail': 'No model loaded'} and both proxies replaced it with 'Frame upscaling failed'; confirmed that was all it was by loading fsrcnn-x2 and getting 200 at 4.7 fps / 214 ms per frame at 480x270 on a CPU-only box. Also two documentation errors found the same way: GET /Upscaler/health is listed and does not exist (only health/detailed), and benchmark-frame is a GET, not a POST. 360 C# + 166 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.26: the plugin downloads the detector itself - tiny-yolov3 is a catalog entry now, so the Models tab fetches and verifies it exactly like an upscaler instead of asking you to bring your own. That became possible only once the pin could be VERIFIED rather than asserted: the file was downloaded, its sha384 checked against the OpenVINO model zoo's own model.yml, and the catalog's sha256 computed from those exact bytes. A REAL MODEL FOUND A REAL BUG: loading the actual tiny-yolov3 on a live server reported input_size 640, because the export declares its spatial dims as ('N', 3, None, None) - nothing in the file says 416 - so the loader used the generic fallback while the anchors are trained for 416. The code was right and the result was wrong; every synthetic test model declares a fixed size, so no test could reach that path. The catalog carries net_size 416 and the loader prefers it. Also two bugs in the catalog sync script, found by running it: it EXECUTED main.py to read the model list (needing fastapi, OpenCV and ONNX Runtime) and had failed outright since v1.8.3.23 with 'attempted relative import' after `from . import object_mask` was added - it parses with ast now; and it would have collapsed the pretty-printed catalog onto one line, because PowerShell captures output as an array and Out-File -NoNewline joins array elements with no separator. 356 C# + 166 Python green.

v1.8.3.25: detection models could not be imported AT ALL - reported in discussion #11 and it was my bug. The import gate hard-required a 4D output, so every detection model was rejected with 'Expected 4D output (N, C, H, W), got shape [1, None, 4]' - the boxes tensor of exactly the yolo-v3-tiny export object masking was built for. v1.8.3.24 could load a detector and mask with it, and there was no way to get one in; every test for that release started from a model already sitting in the models directory, so none walked the path a user walks. The fix is a shared gate rather than an override switch: the importer classifies the model - 4D in and 4D out is an upscaler, otherwise it asks object_mask.plan_for, the SAME function that decides how to drive it at load time. A model that imports is a model that loads; a laxer separate check would only move the rejection to a later step, which is worse because by then the user believes it is installed. An imported detector registers as object-detection with no scale factor, so it stays out of the upscaler dropdowns and auto-mode cannot pick it for a video, and the category survives a container restart. A model that is neither is refused with BOTH readings explained. Six tests cover import to load to mask as one path; against the old gate five of them fail with the reporter's exact message. NOTE: the fix lives in the AI service - update the Docker image too. 354 C# + 166 Python tests green. Also fixes two shutdown bugs found by installing this build on a real server: VideoProcessor released the processing permit as the first statement of its finally block, so on shutdown ObjectDisposedException skipped the rest of the cleanup and a clean stop was logged as a processing failure; and a progress update to an already disposed SessionManager logged a warning with a stack trace on every shutdown with a running job. 356 C# tests green.

v1.8.3.24: object masking now runs DURING PLAYBACK - the part of discussion #11 that v1.8.3.23 did not deliver. That release shipped the masking as a service endpoint nothing called, while the request was for a real-time filter; the user could already produce the result externally, live during playback was the whole point. The player's capture loop already existed for server-side upscaling - it pulls frames off the video element and draws the result onto an overlay - and masking simply had nowhere to send them. Enable it in Settings (classes, box or blur, padding, confidence) plus an admin-gated button that loads the detector, or toggle it live in the player menu under Auto - Cover objects. It REPLACES real-time upscaling while running: upscaling and detecting is two full inference passes per frame, which no realistic server sustains at playback rate, and both surfaces say so rather than letting you discover it as stutter. Batch upscaling is untouched. Padding defaults to 12px because a detector's box hugs the animal and the ears sticking out set a dog off just as well. No detection model ships with the plugin - every catalog entry carries a verified sha256 pin. TESTS THAT CAN ACTUALLY FAIL: mutation testing on v1.8.3.23 found two guards asserting text rather than behaviour - the neighbouring-directory bypass could be fully reintroduced with the suite green (the test asserted the source contained 'rootWithSep', which the bypass leaves in place), and the critical path check was guarded by counting occurrences of IsInsideMediaLibrary( so making the call unreachable kept both the count and the green suite. Both are exercised now: the containment rule is a tested function and ProcessVideo is called with a mocked library manager. The same pass deleted a state field written but never read, and the AI service's masking endpoints are now driven end to end by real synthesised ONNX models, one per detector family. Also: a CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md the contributing page had been linking to while the file did not exist, and every site page showed the current version in the topbar and v1.8.3.13 in the footer - eleven releases stale, because the sync script and the audit both only looked at the topbar. The class list is URL-encoded and confidence formatted invariantly, so 'dog&mode=blur' cannot become a second query parameter and de-DE cannot send 0,35. 354 C# + 160 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.23: object masking, the answer to discussion #11 - a user's dog reacts to dogs and cats on TV and asked for ffmpeg's dnn_detect + drawbox via a custom -vf chain. That cannot work here: jellyfin-ffmpeg's build carries 46 --enable-* flags and no DNN backend at all (no libopenvino/libtensorflow/libtorch, the string 'dnn' does not appear in it), so those filters are absent from the ffmpeg Jellyfin ships whatever the plugin passes. Arbitrary -vf would also be a hole rather than a feature - ffmpeg filter syntax includes movie= and subtitles=, which read files, handing every authenticated user the same primitive v1.8.3.22 just closed on POST /process. So it is done in the AI service, which already loads ONNX models per frame: POST /models/load-detector loads a detector alongside the upscaler rather than instead of it, and POST /detect-mask covers detections with a filled box or a blur, by COCO class or the 'animals' group, with padding because a detector's box hugs the animal and the ears sticking out set a dog off just as well. No detection model ships with it - every catalog entry carries a verified sha256 pin and inventing one would break exactly the guarantee the importer provides, so users bring their own through the existing upload/import path. The decoder handles the v3/v5/v7 and v8/v9 layouts and refuses anything else, because a misread tensor does not throw, it paints boxes over the wrong part of the picture. Also: the face-restore preview proxy read request bodies into the Jellyfin heap unbounded and is now capped at 32 MB, and a static check over the whole AI service asserts every global name its code references exists - written because the detector loader called a helper this service has never had, which Python resolves at call time, so the module imported cleanly and the endpoint would have raised NameError the first time anyone used it. 321 C# + 140 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.22: code-review fixes - one critical and nine confirmed high findings, each re-verified against the code first. SECURITY: POST /process accepted any path on the server (the controller carries only [Authorize] and, unlike its two siblings, had no media-library allowlist) - with ffmpeg's -y an arbitrary-overwrite primitive, plus a file-existence oracle; there is one shared separator-safe allowlist now and neither job entry point overwrites an existing file. AUTO MODE WAS NEVER RUNNING IN BATCH: Model defaulted to realesrgan-x4 while the nightly scan gates on 'auto enabled and model empty or auto', so that gate was always false and every batch run skipped the hardware cap and 8K guard while the dashboard displayed Auto - the default is empty now and the dropdown finally offers Auto. LOCALE: fps= and both -ss values used the current culture, so on de-DE/fr-FR 23.976 became fps=23,976 and a comma is the ffmpeg filter separator - every frame-by-frame job on those servers failed. QUEUE: two permit leaks plus an empty-queue branch that handed the surplus back = 100% of a core after any cancel. Three silent misreports fixed: a Lanczos fallback stored as an AI result (which made the scan filter skip that image forever), an HDR URL that 404'd on a trailing slash while reporting success, and expired cache entries orphaning multi-GB files. And cleanup-dockerhub-tags would have deleted all 71 current tags and re-pointed :latest to a v1.7.8 image - the version is derived from meta.json now. 14 regression guards; 315 C# + 123 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.21: maintainability groundwork - two structural packages, nothing user-facing. model_import.py is a verbatim extraction of the OpenModelDB import and pth->ONNX conversion block from main.py (6808 -> 6627 lines): byte-identical function bodies, no route moved, the endpoints keep their decorators. Three test monkeypatch targets moved with it, and one had been passing for the wrong reason. i18n groundwork makes English a SOURCE language read from Configuration/strings.en.json via a small t() helper - adding a locale is copying the file, translating values and one line of code. Nothing was translated; this phase proves the structure. The scope was cut deliberately: a full extraction is ~485 strings with no user-visible benefit until a translation exists, and the existing UI guard checks element ids rather than text, so a botched sweep would ship silently. 58 keys are migrated - the activity strip and auto-mode texts, all new or rewritten in v1.8.3.20. A missing key renders as the key name rather than an empty string, and t() takes a fallback so the first paint never flashes key names. docs/I18N.md records the numbers and how to continue. 300 C# + 123 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.20: honesty, visibility, reproducibility - five packages, no features. The UI promised 'AI picks model + filter per video' and the code half-kept it: auto stopped overwriting a chosen preset in v1.8.3.14 but still wrote its own whenever the field was empty, so the first playback quietly decided your look. Auto now never writes a filter at all - it offers one in the player's Auto tab and the sidebar with an Apply button, and only when its opinion differs from yours. The activity strip is one line stating phase, frame x of y, model with the auto reason, fps and ETA; those numbers were computed every frame and discarded, and the old 'N jobs completed' counted a list that never contains completed jobs. docs/ENDPOINT-AUDIT.md reports all 66 routes against their real callers (20 unreferenced, grouped by what they are - including six Processing Queue endpoints the settings page configures but no UI ever calls). /Upscaler/hardware-benchmark retires the misleading /Upscaler/recommendations name, which stays as a deprecated alias with an identical payload. Reproducible builds finally are: lock files existed since v1.8.3.13 and no image installed one; five variants now install hash-pinned locks with --require-hashes, and intel and nvidia produced their first lock ever. The Python suite had been red since v1.8.3.14 and shipped over six releases because pytest was not a gate - it is now, and the download path plus the SSRF gate have real coverage. 293 C# + 123 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.19: the Auto tab no longer states a default as a fact. Browser-testing the new tab against the live server caught it reporting 'RUNNING NOW / nomosuni-compact-x2 / HD content in real time' on a page where no video was playing: with no video element the resolver is handed 0x0, falls through to its HD branch, and the pane presented that fallback as a decision about the file in front of you - while also printing the literal string 'unknown output size' as though it were data. Three headings now, matched to what is actually known: 'Running now' when a video is playing and auto is on, 'Auto would pick' when auto is off, and 'Default pick - start playback for this file' when there are no dimensions to decide from. In that last state the output size and the resolution-derived reason are omitted rather than printed, because both would be fabricated; the model, its scale and the signals list stay, because 'Resolution: unknown' is true and useful. Verified in a real browser against the deployed plugin: Auto leads the tab bar, all four switches render their config state, and toggling face restoration flipped EnableFaceRestore, persisted it and re-rendered the pane. 273 tests green.

v1.8.3.18: Auto mode gets its own tab in the player. Auto has been the default since v1.8.3.12, but the in-player panel only ever asked the Custom-mode questions - pick a model, pick a filter - and could not answer the one that matters while a video is running: what did auto decide for THIS file, and how do I turn it off without leaving the player. The panel now leads with an Auto tab showing the model, its scale, the resulting output size, the reason, the signals it looked at and any substitution warning, plus live switches for auto mode, video filters, face restoration and real-time upscaling - each takes effect immediately, and 'Re-apply to this video' re-runs the decision against the running upscaler. The filter row states what is true: auto suggests a look and never overwrites a preset you chose. Docs caught up too: site/configuration.html described auto-selection with models that are not in the catalog (hat-x4, swinir-m-x4, realesrgan-x4plus) and a genre mapping the resolver never had; it now carries the real decision table plus the hardware-budget and scale-ceiling filters. README gains an Auto Mode section. 273 tests green.

v1.8.3.17: 4K sources are cleaned up, not enlarged. TargetScaleFor has answered 1x for sources that are already 4K since v1.8.3.14, but nothing acted on it - only the substitution filter read it and no branch ever produced a 1x pick, so a 4K source still went to 7680x4320. There is now an explicit branch ahead of the multi-frame and anime paths: a 4K source gets a 1x restoration model that removes compression artefacts at the original size. Second cause: the scale parser knew only the 'x<N>' order (realesrgan-x4) and not the '<N>x' order used by the 1x restoration models (dejpg-realplksr-1x) and by every OpenModelDB import (omdb-4x-nomos8k-atd), so every 1x model reported unknown scale; both are parsed now, end-anchored first so realesrgan-x4-256 still means 4x. The overshoot test theory now includes 4K - leaving it out is what hid this - and states the honest invariant: exceeding the target factor must be a reported substitution carrying a reason. 273 tests green.

v1.8.3.16: a substitution must not overshoot the target size. The quality ladder added in v1.8.3.15 picked by weight alone, so a branch that had deliberately chosen a 2x model for 1080p was handed clearreality-x4 - cheap, Light and 4x - producing 7680x4320 with the branch's own reason text ('a 4x pass would target 8K for no visible gain') printed next to it; a 4K source reached 15360x8640. A substitute now has to fit the hardware AND stay within the resolution's target factor, and when nothing satisfies both, the affordable candidate with the smallest scale wins so the overshoot is as small as available. Branch fallbacks are still tried before the ladder, and an id that encodes no scale is not rejected because unknown is not the same as too big. SD keeps its full 4x restore. 270 tests green, including a theory across weak-cpu/strong-cpu/igpu x 720p/1080p x live-action/anime asserting no pick ever exceeds its target factor.

v1.8.3.15: three defects that only a real machine could show, found deploying v1.8.3.14 to a CPU-only server. PreferredAnimeModel shipped with a default of anime-compact-x4, and the resolver cannot tell a shipped default from a deliberate user choice - which is exempt from the hardware budget and the scale logic by design - so EVERY anime decision skipped both and a CPU-only box got a 4x model on 1080p (7680x4320); the default is now empty like its live-action counterpart (saved values are kept: set Preferred Anime Model back to Auto if you never chose one deliberately). The v1.8.3.14 8K fix only covered live action - anime batch still targeted 8K on 1080p. And the budget fallback only walked a branch's own candidates, none of which contain a light model, so on a weak CPU every live-action job collapsed to the last-resort fsrcnn-x2 while clearreality-x4 is equally cheap, does 4x and is ~32x faster than realesrgan-x4 per CPU tile; there is now a quality ladder within each weight class. Reasons describe the material instead of naming a model, so a reason can no longer advertise something that was substituted away. 266 tests green.

v1.8.3.14: Auto mode respects your hardware, and tells the truth about scale. The content heuristic and the AI service's hardware advisor were two separate recommenders that never spoke to each other, so a CPU-only NAS could be handed a full restoration net; the hardware class is now cached and an over-budget pick falls back with a stated reason (an unknown class caps nothing, and a model you picked yourself is never overridden). The service ignores the requested scale and uses the model's native factor, so the library scan logged scale=2x while auto ran a 4x model - a 1080p batch job silently produced 8K frames; the real factor is now read from the model, reported by the API, used by the job, and a 1080p batch no longer defaults to 4x. Every downloadable catalog model gets a Get button (27 of them had none) with real byte progress, and 'Not DL' is split into 'Not downloaded' vs 'Self-host only'. Pause/Resume/Cancel added to the dashboard activity strip. Auto mode no longer overwrites a filter preset you chose. Batch runs log their model reasoning at Information instead of Debug. v1.8.3.1: Cancel-fix (plugin-only, no Docker change). jobs/{id}/cancel reported success but never stopped a running job - VideoProcessor.ProcessVideoAsync created a per-job CancellationTokenSource (the token CancelJob cancels) but passed the bare caller token to the processing pipeline instead of the job's linked cts.Token, so cancellation never reached extraction/upscaling. The semaphore wait, model-load and the method executor now all receive cts.Token (still linked to the caller token), so Cancel stops the job promptly. Pre-existing across all processing methods. Tests: xUnit 164, build clean.

v1.8.3: Opt-in pipeline parallelism (plugin-only, no Docker change). New experimental setting 'Pipeline parallelism' (default OFF) overlaps frame extraction with upscaling instead of running them strictly back-to-back: while ffmpeg is still extracting later frames, already-extracted frames are upscaled concurrently. Built on a thread-safe FrameStreamCoordinator that hands a frame to the upscaler only once a successor frame proves it was fully written, and drops the unproven highest frame if extraction fails, so the output frame-count and ordering are identical to the sequential path. Default behaviour is unchanged; the overlap runs only when the box is ticked. Works with the existing docker7 AI-service images (no rebuild needed). Tests: xUnit 164 (incl. FrameStreamCoordinator COMPLETE-vs-FAILED asymmetry + terminal-first-wins), dotnet build clean.

v1.8.2: Quality + hardening pass. (2) VMAF quality scoring - admin-only POST /Upscaler/vmaf scores an upscaled/distorted file against a reference via ffmpeg+libvmaf (501 if the build lacks libvmaf). (5) Decoupled model download: POST /models/download-async + GET /models/download-status/{id} run big downloads in the background so they no longer trip client/proxy timeouts. v1.7.7: Docker Self-Verification Hardening. Structural completion of the Intel-Arc saga (#45/#66/#67/#69). A dedicated docker-ai-service deep-analysis found no acute bugs left but the MISSING VERIFICATION LAYER that let the whole saga's bug class slip through: no Dockerfile checked at build time whether its expected ONNX provider was actually installed. That gap shipped the v1.7.5 Intel bug (plain onnxruntime built fine, no OpenVINO EP, ran on CPU while dashboard showed GPU). FIX: (1) Dockerfile (NVIDIA) + Dockerfile.intel now assert CUDAExecutionProvider / OpenVINOExecutionProvider after pip install - HARD-FAIL (exit 1) if missing, so a broken GPU image cannot be published. (2) Dockerfile.amd gets a warn-only assert (exit 0, since CPU is a valid AMD fallback when ROCm wheels are yanked) that makes the silent CPU fallback visible in the build log. (3) entrypoint.sh detect_backend() now knows WSL2 /dev/dxg so the startup banner no longer falsely says 'Backend: cpu' on WSL2 setups where main.py correctly detects the GPU. C# Plugin DLL bit-identical to v1.7.6 - all changes in docker-ai-service. Tests 123/123 unchanged. v1.7.x configs bit-compatible.

v1.7.6: Intel OpenVINO Provider Hotfix. Closes the last open Point of issue #69 (Intel Arc GPU detected but inference ran on CPU). Verified empirically via Laurent (FrRene06)'s /gpu-verify output: onnx_providers showed only [AzureExecutionProvider, CPUExecutionProvider] - no OpenVINOExecutionProvider at all. Root cause: requirements-intel.txt had a wrong comment claiming onnxruntime-openvino was deprecated and that plain onnxruntime + system OpenVINO would work; in reality, plain onnxruntime from PyPI does NOT bundle the OpenVINOExecutionProvider, even with system OpenVINO present in the base image. Fix: single-line swap onnxruntime -> onnxruntime-openvino in requirements-intel.txt. After Docker Hub rebuild + container restart, /gpu-verify shows OpenVINOExecutionProvider as active provider and Intel GPU is actually used for inference. C# Plugin DLL bit-identical to v1.7.5 - fix is docker-ai-service-only. Plus AMD build retry (Trivy timeout in v1.7.5 was transient). Tests 123/123 unchanged. v1.7.x configs bit-compatible.

Fix: new EnsureFFmpegReady() in VideoProcessor re-resolves EncoderPath/ProbePath on demand, reconfigures FFMpegCore's GlobalFFOptions, and pushes the resolved paths into all three sub-services via new UpdateFFprobePath() / UpdateFFmpegPath() methods.   - **Native Mode** (default): Direct Radarr/Sonarr API integration for granular control

Moonbase is the Moonfin server plugin for Jellyfin, powering settings sync, the Moonfin Web app at /Moonfin/Web/, a built-in theme editor with custom theme APIs, media bar and ratings integrations, and Seerr proxy/SSO with admin defaults and broadcasts across Moonfin clients.

versions.changelog:
Moonbase 2.2.0 adds server messages, so an admin can write something once and have it show up in people's apps even when they were offline while it was sent. The admin defaults page grows a lot, with settings for another 96 options and fixes to the six controls that were writing values no client reads. Retro games find more of their artwork, and it now picks up new ROMs without a restart. A reinstalled Seerr no longer strands you logged out, and a zipped game now arrives as the ROM it actually is. The bundled web client moves up to Moonfin 2.5.1.

Features:

- A new Messages tab lets an admin write a message with a title and a Markdown body, pick a colour, choose how it shows up, pick who sees it, schedule a start and end date, add a link button, and order the list. Broadcast now saves what it sends, so a user who was offline still finds it.
- Admin defaults picked up settings for another 96 options, covering discovery rows, Since You Watched, music rows, sort direction for the home rows, player buttons, media segments, Cinema Mode for episodes, and a lot more.
- Six admin controls that were writing values no client reads now send the right ones, and row sorting was rebuilt to match the clients, which also adds the missing Playlist Order option.
- Retro games now watch the configured game library folders for file changes, so a new ROM or a per-library scan runs artwork reconciliation in the background instead of waiting for a restart, and games that came out as a false miss are retried once the matching has corrected them.
- The settings sync toggle was renamed to Moonbase Sync, and its description now says that enabling it is required for the Seerr and ratings integrations.
- The bundled web client picks up everything web relevant from Moonfin 2.5.1, including the messages window, a Seerr poster grid with a download progress bar, remote subtitle badges, Play and Resume on the long press menu, and personal ratings writing to Emby.

Bug Fixes:

- A reinstalled Seerr no longer strands you logged out. The plugin was reading every 403 as missing admin rights, so the stale session was never cleared. Now it checks whether Seerr still knows the session first, and a definite refusal clears the old session and signs in again.
- A zipped game now arrives as the ROM it actually is. The detail was naming the archive, so a client saved plain ROM bytes under a .zip name and failed to unpack them. It now names the file the endpoint actually sends, along with its real size.
- A pending artwork timer can no longer take the process down on shutdown, and the artwork delivery route rejects an unknown role instead of falling through.
- The websocket reconnects after a server restart, a busy server no longer reads as a connection timeout, and Escape closes the dialog on top instead of the page behind it.

Moonbase 2.1.0 is mostly about the retro games backend, plus a personal ratings API, audiobook bookmark sync, and the bundled Moonfin web app at 2.5.0.

Features:

- Retro games: arcade ZIPs are validated offline against FBNeo and MAME DAT files, and admins can upload a DAT per core through the plugin.
- Retro games: ROMs are identified by their contents through the libretro RDB databases, with per game core and backend overrides.
- Retro games: a server side artwork pipeline with a manifest, per game artwork priority, and cached thumbnails at the requested size and format. Reconciliation runs on plugin startup and after every library scan.
- Retro games: delivery and per user concurrency limiters, a real Moonfin bridge for the EmulatorJS web player, and archive hashing capped at 512 MB per entry.
- A personal ratings endpoint serves the calling user's ratings in one response, so clients can sort and filter libraries by them.
- Audiobook bookmarks and notes are stored on the server and synced between clients.
- Clients can read their own transcode jobs, so transcoded downloads show real progress and an ETA.
- Settings sync covers everything Moonfin 2.5.0 added: HDR subtitle style, per segment skip actions, home row sort orders, the Studios row, spoiler free toggles, personal rating style, media type badges, segment auto hide, swipe gestures, scroll sensitivity, Cinema Mode for episodes, external trailers, and the crash report toggle.
- Admin defaults page: home row toggles with per row sorting defaults, Seerr Watchlist and Seerr shortcuts rows, the Aya media bar style, a Recently Released series type default, and pushing a genre, collection, or playlist row now enables its category toggle.
- The plugin reports itself as Moonbase throughout the dashboard.

Bug Fixes:

- TV studios get their logos, since TMDB networks are now read alongside production companies. Network ids are namespaced apart from company ids and the logo cache index is versioned.
- Seerr provisioning reports why it stopped instead of a bare status.
- IMDb charts stopped returning 403.
- Admin defaults: browsing and details blur defaults no longer fail the whole save, the theme music volume default is saved, and the Continue Watching image type options send values the client understands.

Web App:

- Bundles Moonfin 2.5.0 with the first run setup wizard, the Aya media bar, the full set of library sorts and filters, personal ratings, Seerr browse shortcuts, a Live TV favorites row, a Studio row, Live TV series recording, spoiler free toggles, an expanded metadata editor, Vim style playback keys, per segment skip actions, an HDR subtitle style, and crash reports sent to your own server.
- Fixes for playback control flicker, the skip button, subtitle offset range, Seerr row hover and localization, Continue Watching and Next Up paging, library search with Group By, blurry search posters, context menu placement, studio logo matching, media bar gradient flashing, backdrop fades, source pickers losing ids, book summaries, right to left layouts, and internationalized server domain names.

Features:

- Added a Playback tab to the admin defaults page, covering autoplay, audio and subtitle language, subtitle mode, skip lengths, intro action, still watching behavior, Next Up timeout, and rewind durations.
- Added default pickers for Action Buttons and Seerr Discovery row order.
- Added profile properties for OLED mode, the player time labels, and the new home row options, so those settings sync between devices.
- Game ROM and BIOS routes answer HEAD requests, which is how clients check a file's size before downloading it.

Bug Fixes:

- The Playback admin tab now writes the keys, values, and units clients actually read. Several pickers were saving under names no client looked for, so those defaults silently did nothing.
- Resume Rewind and Unpause Rewind options match what the client offers, instead of listing durations it has no setting for.
- Removed admin controls that no longer map to anything a client syncs. The underlying profile properties stay in place, so device to device sync is unaffected.
- Fixed the label text on the Details Screen Blur setting.

Features:

- Push notifications now reach Moonfin apps even when they're closed, covering Seerr activity, new media added to your library, and admin broadcasts. Admins can point at a self-hosted relay or their own FCM service account.
- Custom home rows sync across device profiles, so a row you build on one device shows up on the others, and edits and deletions carry over.
- Added a Max Days in Next Up setting.
- MDBList gained a Test Key button that shows your plan and remaining quota, a Clear Cache button, a max items limit for official lists, and Roger Ebert as a rating source.
- Added button layout sync so clients keep their player and details button layouts per device type.
- Glass and 8-bit Hero joined the admin default theme picker, along with the 8-bit Gold accent.

Bug Fixes:

- Fixed MDBList rows dropping shows, since the item cap was applied unevenly across the separate movie and show lists.
- Fixed Rotten Tomatoes critic scores never matching.
- MDBList rate limits are handled properly now, with your quota checked before syncing and partial results kept instead of overwriting good cached data.
- Ratings are filtered by the requesting device's profile instead of always using the global one.
- Fixed the Ping response casing that made clients report Seerr as not configured, and Emby media bar items now come back in the shape clients expect.
- Fixed the Emby plugin settings page never loading.
- Cancelling a Seerr request you don't have permission to cancel no longer logs you out of Seerr.
- The settings updated broadcast only fires when a save actually changed something, which stops sync loops between devices.
- Fixed the Seerr media available webhook breaking on some Jellyfin versions.

Features:

- Added password-less Seerr sign in through a Quick Connect bridge, so users who log in with Quick Connect get signed into Seerr silently.
- Added a server-side Radarr and Sonarr calendar proxy so clients can show upcoming release calendars, reachable for non-admin accounts too.
- Widened settings sync from 87 synced settings to 207, backed by new settings profile properties.

- On Emby, Moonfin web assets are now served with an explicit content type so the frontend loads correctly.

versions.changelog:
- Fix the banner covering the top navigation on Jellyfin 12.0's new "modern" UI. JellyFlare now detects the layout and pushes the nav bar and content down instead of drawing over them. 10.11 and TV unchanged. (fixes #12)

**Jellyfin 12.0:** you don't need the File Transformation plugin. JavaScript Injector injects the banner on its own. If you kept File Transformation from 10.11, remove it: its current build isn't 12.0-compatible and, while installed, stops the banner from injecting.

Thanks to @nothing2obvi for the report and for confirming the File Transformation behaviour on 12.0. ❤️

- Add per-banner link popup hint: each rotation message and permanent entry can now carry its own optional hint text shown above the Open/Copy/Cancel buttons, overriding the global default. Per-banner hint → global default → nothing (when both empty). Existing setups keep working unchanged. The Settings-tab field is relabeled "Default link popup hint" to reflect the fallback (requested by @nerdc0re-net #9)

- Fix maintenance mode error 500 on Jellyfin 10.11.10: `IUserManager.Users` was removed and replaced by `GetUsers()`; the plugin now compiles against the 10.11.10 SDK so the call resolves correctly (thanks @LRoffic for the report — #11)
- Bump minimum supported Jellyfin version to 10.11.10 (users on 10.11.6-10.11.9 could stay on v1.15.1 until they update Jellyfin)

- Fix banner not showing on Jellyfin instances configured with a base URL (e.g. `/jellyfin`); plugin fetches now go through `ApiClient.getUrl()` so the base URL is honored (thanks @Kayoku and @FazeThree71 for the report — #10)
- Add Monthly schedule type for banners: target the nth weekday of every month (e.g. "second Tuesday", "last Friday"), with an optional time window

- Add per-user banner muting: users can hide the rotating and/or permanent banner for their own account from their Jellyfin Display settings
- Per-account preference syncs across devices and live across open tabs; maintenance mode is never affected
- Add admin master switch to allow/forbid user muting, plus a configurable warning text (Settings tab)

- Add limit on link preview size
- Add option for comment on link popup

- Fix copy and open link in Jellyfin Media Player on desktop not working
- Update CI to avoid overwriting releases

- Add route filtering on each banner
- Add new project status in the README: project stays active but has reach a satisfying state and stays opens to bug report and feature requests but will not be as proactive as in its early development

- Add scheduling for maintenance mode and restart
- Improve UX for maintenance tab
- Add documentation link to the config page
- Add dependency warning on the config page as a warning banner

- (Tested, but use it with caution) Add a maintenance tab to let you work on your instance without user connecting to the server
- Add preview of affected users (maintenance)
- Add a reset button (maintenance) and link it to the global reset button
- Adjust dismiss button font sizes based on config settings
- Fixed close button visibility logic based on config

- Fixed the "hide all" configuration not being effective
- Added issue templates

Important changes:

- Update manifest description
- Add refresh prompt on each save
- Improve reset mechanism clarity with three distinct buttons and updated labels alongside alerts to save the config
- Improve alert rendering on misconfiguration on input validation
- Regroup isolated settings into Behavior category
- Dismissing a message, all messages, or the permanent banner now syncs instantly to other open tabs via a BroadcastChannel.
- Remove or update legacy code from first implementation

Various refactoring, safety and robustness fixes detailed below:

- `TextAlign` and `TransitionSpeed` are now whitelisted on save; invalid values normalise to `"center"` / `"normal"` rather than being stored verbatim.
- `parseInt` calls in `checkTimeWindow` now always pass radix `10`, preventing silent misparses on malformed time strings.
- Invalid-date checks for fixed schedules use `isNaN(date.getTime())` instead of `isNaN(date)` for clarity.
- `closeBtn.innerHTML` replaced with `closeBtn.textContent` for consistency with the rest of the codebase.
- Token retrieval deduplicated into a single `getToken()` helper used at both call sites.
- French tooltip text on the close and dismiss-all buttons replaced with English equivalents.
- Fixed a 50 ms race where the rotation timer could fire `tick()` before the navigation debounce resolved. The timer is now cleared immediately at the top of `onNavigate()` when `showInDashboard` is `false`.
- Plugin startup now gives up after a fixed retry count instead of looping indefinitely.
- Save endpoint rejects dangerous URL schemes (`javascript:` etc.) in both rotation and permanent entries.
- Save endpoint validates schedule types and returns a clear error for unknown values instead of silently defaulting to "always".
- Numeric settings (durations, banner height, active index) are clamped to their allowed ranges on save.
- Config changes are picked up on the next page navigation instead of waiting for the old rotation queue to finish.
- Layout recalculation now batches all reads before all writes, avoiding repeated forced reflows.
- Resize observer on the header is re-attached on every banner show, preventing stale references from rapid hide/show cycles.
- Rotation-message and permanent-entry row builders (~460 lines of duplicated code) replaced with a single shared factory function.
- Default presets, rotation messages, and permanent entries consolidated into one `CONFIG_DEFAULTS` object.
- Each Settings subsection (Appearance, Timing, Controls, Behaviour, Presets) has its own reset function; Reset and Wipe buttons delegate to these.
- Row-field collection extracted into a single shared helper used by both collect functions.
- Default text colour normalised to `#ffffff` in the data model for both rotation and permanent entries.
- Magic numbers in the banner script replaced with named constants (`BANNER_Z_INDEX`, `POPUP_Z_INDEX`, `MOBILE_BREAKPOINT`, etc.).
- Add drag and drop feature to messages collections
- Permanent banner can now optionally be dismissed, persistence behavior can be configured
- The app now tries to open link outside the in-app web browser framework, but for unsupported platform also let the user copy the url (better transparency)

- Fixed banner animation hiding first carousel arrows and title
- Added new default rotation entry
- Banner in dashboard visibility defaults to false and is set at the bottom of the config page
- Normalise line endings to inside jq before the value touches the shell

- Improved admin dashboard detection, add warning for the visibility option
- Fixed XSS vector: banner link URLs are now validated against an allowlist (https://, http://, /); any other scheme including javascript: is silently rejected
- Fixed privilege escalation: the config save endpoint (POST /JellyFlare/config) now requires admin-level credentials (RequiresElevation policy); standard user tokens are rejected
- Config and script endpoints now require authentication; unauthenticated visitors receive no banner and cannot read plugin configuration: the plugin is intended for registered users only, consistent with JS Injector
- CI actions pinned to full commit SHAs to eliminate supply-chain risk from re-tagged upstream actions
- change permanent docs image.

- add configurable sizes for dismiss buttons in settings;
- add option to show banner in admin dashboard.

- permanent banner can be disabled but still saved;
- add customization to hide all button and close button.
- add quick access to the plugin from the dashboard sidebar
- first version, may be unstable

description:
Authenticate your Jellyfin with Authelia, and optionally create users who do not yet exist automatically.
This plugin uses Authelia HTTP API for authentication. Unlike with an SSO plugin, this allows using the existing Jellyfin login UI and API, which is compatible with all existing Jellyfin clients.
The main drawback of this approach is that 2FA is not supported.
